# Lucifer's Diary

A personal writing platform — a dark literary publication site for serious long-form writing.

This is a monorepo containing two packages:

- **`backend/`** — NestJS + Prisma + PostgreSQL API (port 3001)
- **`frontend/`** — Next.js App Router app — public reading site + admin panel (port 3000)

## Documentation

- [`docs/PROJECT.md`](docs/PROJECT.md) — complete build specification (architecture, data model, API routes, business rules)
- `Lucifer's Diary Design System/` — color tokens, typography, component specs, brand voice
- `lucife'r sdiary Hi-Fi design/` — interactive hi-fi mockups and original design brief

## Surfaces

- **Public site** (`/`) — readers browse stories and series, read them, and leave anonymous likes (no account required)
- **Admin panel** (`/admin`) — single-author authoring tool, JWT-protected by a shared password

## Tech stack

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Backend API | NestJS + Prisma + PostgreSQL |
| Frontend | Next.js (App Router) |
| Auth | Single admin password → JWT |
| Styling | CSS Modules + Tailwind (shadcn internals only) |
| UI Components | shadcn/ui |
| Animations | GSAP + ScrollTrigger |
| Animated Icons | AnimateUI |

## Running locally

```bash
# Backend (port 3001)
cd backend
npm install
npx prisma migrate dev
npm run start:dev

# Frontend (port 3000)
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

The public site is served at `http://localhost:3000`; the admin panel is at `http://localhost:3000/admin`.

## Deploying

End-to-end aaPanel runbook — Node.js + PM2 + Nginx + PostgreSQL — lives in [`DEPLOY.md`](DEPLOY.md).

Relevant moving parts:

- [`ecosystem.config.js`](ecosystem.config.js) — PM2 manifest. Boots both apps, runs `prisma migrate deploy` on the API.
- [`deploy/nginx.conf.example`](deploy/nginx.conf.example) — Nginx site config. Proxies `/api/*` to the backend, everything else to Next.js, with cache headers on `_next/static/`.
- [`backend/.env.example`](backend/.env.example) and [`frontend/.env.local.example`](frontend/.env.local.example) — env templates.
- `GET /api/health` — liveness probe (no DB call).
- `GET /api/health/ready` — readiness probe (round-trips Postgres).

content.content:
1	# Deploying Lucifer's Diary on aaPanel
2	
3	End-to-end runbook for putting the site on an aaPanel VPS. Assumes
4	you already have a domain pointed at the server and Node.js + PM2 +
5	Nginx + PostgreSQL installed via aaPanel's app store.
6	
7	## 1. Prepare the server
8	
9	In aaPanel, install (one-time):
10	
11	- **Node.js 20** (App Store → Node.js Version Manager → install 20)
12	- **PostgreSQL 16+** (App Store → PostgreSQL Manager)
13	- **PM2** (comes with Node.js Version Manager; or `npm i -g pm2`)
14	- **Nginx** (already installed on a fresh aaPanel)
15	
16	Open a terminal (aaPanel sidebar → Terminal) and confirm:
17	
18	```bash
19	node -v       # v20.x
20	npm -v
21	psql --version
22	pm2 -v
23	```
24	
25	## 2. Create the database
26	
27	In aaPanel → Databases → Add Database (PostgreSQL):
28	
29	- Database name: `lucifer_diary`
30	- Username: `lucifer`
31	- Password: pick a long random string
32	
33	Note the connection string — it'll be:
34	
35	```
36	postgresql://lucifer:PASSWORD@localhost:5432/lucifer_diary
37	```
38	
39	## 3. Pull the code
40	
41	In aaPanel → Files, navigate to `/www/wwwroot/` and clone:
42	
43	```bash
44	cd /www/wwwroot
45	git clone https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/lucifers-diary.git luciferdiary
46	cd luciferdiary
47	```
48	
49	(Use HTTPS + a personal access token if the repo is private.)
50	
51	## 4. Configure environment variables
52	
53	### Backend
54	
55	```bash
56	cp backend/.env.example backend/.env
57	nano backend/.env
58	```
59	
60	Set:
61	
62	- `DATABASE_URL` — the string from step 2
63	- `ADMIN_PASSWORD` — your admin login password
64	- `JWT_SECRET` — generate with `node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(48).toString('hex'))"`
65	- `PORT` — `3001` (matches the Nginx config)
66	- `FRONTEND_URL` — `https://YOUR_DOMAIN,https://www.YOUR_DOMAIN`
67	
68	### Frontend
69	
70	```bash
71	cp frontend/.env.local.example frontend/.env.local
72	nano frontend/.env.local
73	```
74	
75	Set:
76	
77	- `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` — `https://YOUR_DOMAIN/api`
78	- `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` — `https://YOUR_DOMAIN` (no trailing slash)
79	
80	> **NEXT_PUBLIC_\* values are inlined at build time** — re-run the
81	> frontend build after changing them.
82	
83	## 5. Install + build
84	
85	From the repo root:
86	
87	```bash
88	# Backend
89	cd backend
90	npm ci
91	npx prisma migrate deploy        # applies every migration in order
92	npx prisma generate              # regenerate the client
93	npm run build                    # tsc -> dist/
94	npm run seed:tags                # OPTIONAL: seed the 591-tag taxonomy
95	
96	# Frontend
97	cd ../frontend
98	npm ci
99	npm run build                    # produces .next/
100	```
101	
102	## 6. Run with PM2
103	
104	From the repo root:
105	
106	```bash
107	pm2 start ecosystem.config.js
108	pm2 save                          # persist across reboots
109	pm2 startup systemd               # follow the printed `sudo` command
110	```
111	
112	Sanity-check both apps came up:
113	
114	```bash
115	pm2 ls
116	curl http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/health
117	curl http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/health/ready    # checks DB connectivity
118	curl -I http://127.0.0.1:3000/                 # Next homepage
119	```
120	
121	## 7. Nginx reverse proxy
122	
123	In aaPanel → Website → **Add Site** → enter your domain. After it
124	creates the site:
125	
126	- Open the site's "Config File" tab
127	- Replace the contents with `deploy/nginx.conf.example` from this repo
128	- Replace `YOUR_DOMAIN` and `/www/wwwroot/luciferdiary/frontend` with
129	  your actual values
130	- Save and reload Nginx
131	
132	In aaPanel → Website → SSL → **Apply for SSL** → Let's Encrypt. Tick
133	both `YOUR_DOMAIN` and `www.YOUR_DOMAIN`. aaPanel will rewrite the
134	config to listen on 443 and add the cert paths automatically — the
135	location rules from `nginx.conf.example` survive intact.
136	
137	## 8. Smoke test
138	
139	Visit `https://YOUR_DOMAIN`. You should see:
140	
141	- The homepage with a sticky header (logo · search · controls)
142	- `/admin/login` lets you in with `ADMIN_PASSWORD`
143	- `/api/health` returns `{"status":"ok"}`
144	- `/sitemap.xml` lists every published URL
145	- `/feed.xml` validates as Atom
146	
147	## 9. Updating
148	
149	Each time you push a new commit:
150	
151	```bash
152	cd /www/wwwroot/luciferdiary
153	git pull
154	
155	# Backend
156	cd backend
157	npm ci                            # only re-runs install when the lockfile changed
158	npx prisma migrate deploy         # picks up any new migrations
159	npm run build                     # tsc -> dist/
160	
161	# Frontend — `rebuild` wipes .next/ so old chunk hashes don't linger
162	cd ../frontend
163	npm ci
164	npm run rebuild
165	
166	# Restart both
167	pm2 restart ecosystem.config.js
168	```
169	
170	> **Cache note:** the CMS HTML is served with `Cache-Control: no-store`
171	> via `next.config.ts`, so admin pages always fetch fresh after a
172	> rebuild. Public pages keep their default revalidation behavior, and
173	> hashed chunks under `/_next/static/` stay `immutable`. If a writer
174	> still sees a blank CMS after deploy, hard-reload (Ctrl+Shift+R) once
175	> — the immutable chunks are fine to keep, only the stale HTML needs
176	> to clear.
177	
178	---
179	
180	## Troubleshooting
181	
182	**`prisma migrate deploy` says no schema** — make sure you're inside
183	`backend/` when running it. The schema is at `backend/prisma/schema.prisma`.
184	
185	**`502 Bad Gateway`** — PM2 isn't running, or it's crashed. Check
186	`pm2 logs lucifer-api --lines 100` and `pm2 logs lucifer-web --lines 100`.
187	
188	**Admin login returns 401** — the `JWT_SECRET` in `.env` doesn't

# Deploying Lucifer's Diary on aaPanel

End-to-end runbook for putting the site on an aaPanel VPS. Assumes
you already have a domain pointed at the server and Node.js + PM2 +
Nginx + PostgreSQL installed via aaPanel's app store.

## 1. Prepare the server

In aaPanel, install (one-time):

- **Node.js 20** (App Store → Node.js Version Manager → install 20)
- **PostgreSQL 16+** (App Store → PostgreSQL Manager)
- **PM2** (comes with Node.js Version Manager; or `npm i -g pm2`)
- **Nginx** (already installed on a fresh aaPanel)

Open a terminal (aaPanel sidebar → Terminal) and confirm:

```bash
node -v       # v20.x
npm -v
psql --version
pm2 -v
```

## 2. Create the database

In aaPanel → Databases → Add Database (PostgreSQL):

- Database name: `lucifer_diary`
- Username: `lucifer`
- Password: pick a long random string

Note the connection string — it'll be:

```
postgresql://lucifer:PASSWORD@localhost:5432/lucifer_diary
```

## 3. Pull the code

In aaPanel → Files, navigate to `/www/wwwroot/` and clone:

```bash
cd /www/wwwroot
git clone https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/lucifers-diary.git luciferdiary
cd luciferdiary
```

(Use HTTPS + a personal access token if the repo is private.)

## 4. Configure environment variables

### Backend

```bash
cp backend/.env.example backend/.env
nano backend/.env
```

Set:

- `DATABASE_URL` — the string from step 2
- `ADMIN_PASSWORD` — your admin login password
- `JWT_SECRET` — generate with `node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(48).toString('hex'))"`
- `PORT` — `3001` (matches the Nginx config)
- `FRONTEND_URL` — `https://YOUR_DOMAIN,https://www.YOUR_DOMAIN`

### Frontend

```bash
cp frontend/.env.local.example frontend/.env.local
nano frontend/.env.local
```

Set:

- `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` — `https://YOUR_DOMAIN/api`
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` — `https://YOUR_DOMAIN` (no trailing slash)

> **NEXT_PUBLIC_\* values are inlined at build time** — re-run the
> frontend build after changing them.

## 5. Install + build

From the repo root:

```bash
# Backend
cd backend
npm ci
npx prisma migrate deploy        # applies every migration in order
npx prisma generate              # regenerate the client
npm run build                    # tsc -> dist/
npm run seed:tags                # OPTIONAL: seed the 591-tag taxonomy

# Frontend
cd ../frontend
npm ci
npm run build                    # produces .next/
```

## 6. Run with PM2

From the repo root:

```bash
pm2 start ecosystem.config.js
pm2 save                          # persist across reboots
pm2 startup systemd               # follow the printed `sudo` command
```

Sanity-check both apps came up:

```bash
pm2 ls
curl http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/health
curl http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/health/ready    # checks DB connectivity
curl -I http://127.0.0.1:3000/                 # Next homepage
```

## 7. Nginx reverse proxy

In aaPanel → Website → **Add Site** → enter your domain. After it
creates the site:

- Open the site's "Config File" tab
- Replace the contents with `deploy/nginx.conf.example` from this repo
- Replace `YOUR_DOMAIN` and `/www/wwwroot/luciferdiary/frontend` with
  your actual values
- Save and reload Nginx

In aaPanel → Website → SSL → **Apply for SSL** → Let's Encrypt. Tick
both `YOUR_DOMAIN` and `www.YOUR_DOMAIN`. aaPanel will rewrite the
config to listen on 443 and add the cert paths automatically — the
location rules from `nginx.conf.example` survive intact.

## 8. Smoke test

Visit `https://YOUR_DOMAIN`. You should see:

- The homepage with a sticky header (logo · search · controls)
- `/admin/login` lets you in with `ADMIN_PASSWORD`
- `/api/health` returns `{"status":"ok"}`
- `/sitemap.xml` lists every published URL
- `/feed.xml` validates as Atom

## 9. Updating

Each time you push a new commit:

```bash
cd /www/wwwroot/luciferdiary
git pull

# Backend
cd backend
npm ci                            # only re-runs install when the lockfile changed
npx prisma migrate deploy         # picks up any new migrations
npm run build                     # tsc -> dist/

# Frontend — `rebuild` wipes .next/ so old chunk hashes don't linger
cd ../frontend
npm ci
npm run rebuild

# Restart both
pm2 restart ecosystem.config.js
```

> **Cache note:** the CMS HTML is served with `Cache-Control: no-store`
> via `next.config.ts`, so admin pages always fetch fresh after a
> rebuild. Public pages keep their default revalidation behavior, and
> hashed chunks under `/_next/static/` stay `immutable`. If a writer
> still sees a blank CMS after deploy, hard-reload (Ctrl+Shift+R) once
> — the immutable chunks are fine to keep, only the stale HTML needs
> to clear.

---

## Troubleshooting

**`prisma migrate deploy` says no schema** — make sure you're inside
`backend/` when running it. The schema is at `backend/prisma/schema.prisma`.

**`502 Bad Gateway`** — PM2 isn't running, or it's crashed. Check
`pm2 logs lucifer-api --lines 100` and `pm2 logs lucifer-web --lines 100`.

**Admin login returns 401** — the `JWT_SECRET` in `.env` doesn't
match the one used to sign existing tokens. Clear localStorage in
your browser and log in again, or rotate to a fresh secret.

**`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` change doesn't take effect** — those are
baked in at build time. Re-run `npm run build` in `frontend/` after
editing `.env.local`, then `pm2 restart lucifer-web`.

**Hostname or DNS error from Prisma** — the database isn't reachable
from the API process. Try `psql "$DATABASE_URL"` with the same env;
fix the connection string until that succeeds.

**Migrations diverged on a fresh DB** — only run `prisma migrate
deploy`. Never run `prisma migrate dev` or `prisma db push` against
production; they can drop columns.

**Blank CMS / `ChunkLoadError` after deploy** — the browser is
holding onto cached HTML that references chunks the new build
deleted. The CMS is configured `Cache-Control: no-store` so this
should self-heal on next request, but if a tab was already open
during the rebuild, hard-reload it (Ctrl+Shift+R). To prevent it
entirely, use `npm run rebuild` (wipes `.next/` first) and
`pm2 restart lucifer-web` in that order.

content.text:
Here's the full walkthrough. I read through your actual SEO code, and the honest headline is: **your site is already ~95% done on the technical side.** The remaining work is mostly *operational* (things you do in Google's tools) plus one config gotcha that can silently break everything.

---

## First, set expectations honestly

These are two very different goals:

- **"Visible in Google"** → getting *indexed*. This is mechanical, you fully control it, and it takes days-to-weeks. Totally achievable.
- **"One of the first results"** → *ranking*. This is competitive and **cannot be guaranteed by anyone**. For your own brand name ("Lucifer's Diary") you can realistically rank #1 within weeks — though note you're competing with the TV show *Lucifer*, so the exact title + your domain matter. For generic terms ("dark fiction", "short horror") it's a months-to-years game driven by content volume, backlinks, and authority. Anyone promising guaranteed #1 for competitive terms is lying.

---

## What you already have (genuinely strong)

| Signal | Status | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `robots.txt` (allows all, blocks `/admin`, points to sitemap) | ✅ | `app/robots.ts` |
| Dynamic `sitemap.xml` (home, stories, series, chapters, tags; hourly refresh) | ✅ | `app/sitemap.ts` |
| Rich metadata (canonical, title templates, `index:true`) | ✅ | `app/layout.tsx` |
| Open Graph + Twitter cards | ✅ | layout |
| Auto-generated OG images (default + per story/chapter/series) | ✅ | `app/*/opengraph-image.tsx` |
| JSON-LD structured data: `WebSite`, `Article`, `CreativeWorkSeries`, `BreadcrumbList` | ✅ | layout + page files |
| Atom feed, PWA manifest | ✅ | `app/feed.xml`, `app/manifest.ts` |
| Server-rendered HTML (crawlers see content on first request) | ✅ | — |

This is better SEO plumbing than most sites ship with. You don't need to *build* much — you need to *activate* it.

---

## The one thing that can silently kill all of it ⚠️

Every URL Google sees — canonical tags, sitemap entries, OG `url`, JSON-LD — is built from `SITE_URL`, which reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` and **defaults to `http://localhost:3000`** (`lib/site.ts:7`). And `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values are **baked in at build time**, not read at runtime.

**So:** if the production build wasn't done with `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` set to your real domain, every link Google indexes points to `localhost` → your site is effectively invisible.

**Verify in 30 seconds** once it's live — open these and confirm the URLs inside say your real domain, *not* localhost:
- `https://YOUR_DOMAIN/sitemap.xml`
- `https://YOUR_DOMAIN/robots.txt`
- View-source on the homepage → check `<link rel="canonical">` and `og:url`

If they say localhost: fix `frontend/.env.local`, **rebuild**, restart. (This is in your `DEPLOY.md` §4, but it's the #1 thing people miss.)

---

## The actual steps to get found

**Step 1 — Google Search Console** (the single most important action)
1. Go to [search.google.com/search-console](https://search.google.com/search-console), add your domain as a property.
2. **Verify ownership** — easiest is a DNS TXT record, or an HTML meta tag (← I can add this tag to your code in one small PR).
3. **Submit your sitemap**: enter `sitemap.xml`.
4. Use **URL Inspection → Request Indexing** on your homepage + a few top stories to jump the crawl queue.

**Step 2 — Bing Webmaster Tools** ([bing.com/webmasters](https://www.bing.com/webmasters)) — covers Bing *and* ChatGPT/Copilot search. You can one-click import from Search Console.

**Step 3 — Confirm it's working** — after a few days, search `site:YOUR_DOMAIN` on Google. Whatever shows up is what's indexed. Watch the **Pages** report in Search Console for errors.

**Step 4 — Ranking (the long game)** — what actually moves the needle: publish regularly, get real backlinks (links from relevant sites/communities matter most), strong page titles + meta descriptions, fast mobile pages. Your tags/series already give good internal linking.

---

## What I can do in code (through our `develop` workflow)

The most useful additions I can make as PRs into `develop`:

1. **Google + Bing site-verification meta tags** via Next's `metadata.verification` — turns Search Console verification into one click. *(Needs your verification codes, or we skip it and you verify via DNS.)*
2. **Enrich the `Article` schema** with `datePublished` / `dateModified` / `wordCount` / `image` if missing — improves rich-result eligibility.
3. **An author/about page** to strengthen E-E-A-T (Google's author-credibility signals).

To get started, two questions:
- **What's the production domain?** (so I can sanity-check `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` and tailor everything)
- Want me to kick off **#1 (verification meta tags)** as the first addition into `develop`? If so, set up the Search Console property and grab the verification code, or tell me you'd rather verify by DNS.

Checked it thoroughly — and here's the verdict:

## ✅ Localhost is NOT the problem. Nothing to fix there.

The live site is correctly configured. Evidence from `https://lucifersdiary.com` right now:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `robots.txt` | ✅ `Allow: /`, points to real sitemap |
| `sitemap.xml` URLs | ✅ all `https://lucifersdiary.com/...` (not localhost) |

So `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` *was* set at build time. The technical SEO is genuinely live and correct. No code change needed for this.

---

## ⚠️ But I found the real ceiling on your goal — and it's not technical

Your sitemap tags are: `adult`, `cuckquean`, `exhibitionism`, `dom-sub-switch`, etc. **This is explicit adult content.** That has a huge, unavoidable effect on "being one of the first search results":

- **Google SafeSearch filters explicit content out of results entirely** for any user with SafeSearch on — which is the default for signed-out users in many regions, mandatory for minors, and common on shared/work networks. For that large share of searchers, your pages **won't appear at all**, regardless of ranking.
- For general (non-explicit) queries, Google **actively demotes** adult content unless the query clearly seeks it.

This doesn't block *indexing* — your pages can still be found by people deliberately searching adult terms with SafeSearch off. But "rank #1 for broad searches" is effectively capped by Google's policy, not by anything we can fix in code. I'd be doing you a disservice not to say that plainly up front.

---

Since the plumbing is correct, the real blocker to visibility is simply that **you haven't told Google to crawl it yet.** The highest-leverage next step is **Google Search Console**: verify the domain, submit the sitemap, request indexing.

message.content: before we do any of that can you explain what back links are.

content.text:
A backlink is simply **a link on someone else's website that points to yours.** If a blog writes "check out this story at lucifersdiary.com" and links it, that's one backlink to your site. That's the whole mechanic — but *why they matter* is the interesting part.

## Why Google cares about them

Google's founding insight (literally the algorithm that made Google win, called PageRank) was this: **treat a link as a vote.** If lots of other sites link to you, you're probably worth showing. A link is one site vouching for another.

So backlinks are the main way Google measures **authority** — how trustworthy and important your site is, beyond just what *you* say about yourself. You can write "best erotica on the web" in your own title all day; that's you talking about yourself. A *backlink* is someone *else* effectively saying it. Google trusts the second one far more.

## Not all backlinks are equal

This is the part that matters most:

- **Quality beats quantity, by a lot.** One link from a big, relevant, trusted site is worth more than hundreds from junk sites. A link from a popular erotica forum or a well-known adult-fiction directory is gold. A link from some random auto-generated spam page is worth ~nothing — and a pile of those can actively *hurt* you.
- **Relevance matters.** A link from an erotica community helps your erotica site more than a link from a car-parts blog.
- **"dofollow" vs "nofollow."** Some links carry ranking power ("dofollow"); others are tagged so Google ignores them for ranking ("nofollow" — most social media and comment links are these). Nofollow links still bring *visitors*, which is valuable, but pass little authority.

## Why this is the thing standing between you and the head terms

Remember I said Literotica/Reddit/Wattpad are unbeatable on "sex stories"? **Backlinks are why.** Over 20+ years they've each accumulated *millions* of backlinks from across the web. That's an authority mountain a new domain can't climb quickly, no matter how good your on-page SEO is. On-page work (what I'm about to do) makes you *eligible* to rank; backlinks are what let you actually *outrank* established competitors.

## What building them looks like for *your* site (honestly)

For an adult site, the normal mainstream avenues (news sites, mainstream blogs) are mostly closed, so it's a specific game:
- **Adult-content directories** that list erotica sites.
- **Communities & forums** where erotica readers gather (Reddit, niche forums, Discords) — engage genuinely, link where it's welcome.
- **Social profiles** (Bluesky, X, etc.) — mostly "nofollow" so little ranking juice, but they drive real readers and discovery.
- **Other authors / cross-promotion** — link exchanges with peer sites in the niche.

⚠️ **One firm warning:** do **not** buy bulk backlinks from "1000 links for $20" services. Google detects unnatural link patterns and can *penalize* (de-rank) your site for it. Slow and genuine beats fast and spammy — and a manual penalty is very hard to recover from.

---

The short version: **on-page SEO (my job, starting now) gets you in the race; backlinks (your slow, ongoing job) determine how far up you finish.** For your *brand name* you barely need them — you'll rank for "Lucifer's Diary" on relevance alone. For competitive terms, they're everything.

### Your request, mapped to what's already there

Go to any story page and select 20+ characters of text — a floating bar pops up with **5 buttons**:

| You asked for | Existing button | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Floating bar on text select | *(the popover itself)* | Appears on selection, clamps to screen edges, dismisses on Esc/scroll/click-away |

| "Share to social with link attached" | **X**, **Facebook**, **Bluesky** | Opens the share composer pre-filled with the quote + link |

### One genuine improvement that fits your strategy perfectly

There *is* a worthwhile gap. Right now the **social buttons (X/FB/Bluesky) attach the plain page URL** — but the **Copy Link to Passage** button is the one that makes the deep-link to the exact spot. Since your whole plan is *"post quotes elsewhere with links back,"* it'd be much better if the **social shares also used the deep-link**, so anyone clicking from Reddit/X lands directly on the highlighted passage instead of the top of the page. Small change, high payoff for exactly what you're doing.

- **Most Reddit links are `nofollow`**, so they pass little direct ranking authority. They drive real *readers* (valuable!) and indirect signals, but they're not the backlink authority that moves competitive rankings.
- **Watch subreddit self-promo rules** — many ban or rate-limit linking to your own site (karma gates, the "90/10" rule). Drop links genuinely inside real engagement, or you'll get shadowbanned.
- Best venues: niche adult-fiction subreddits, dedicated forums, and **adult-fiction directories** (those directory links are more often `dofollow` — better for authority).

That distinction matters, because what you described — a dedicated page whose CTA takes you to the *current* content homepage — is a **gateway/splash** pattern, which is subtly different and usually worse:

| | One rich homepage (Literotica's actual model) | Gateway page → content elsewhere |
|---|---|---|
| Clicks to content | 0 — scroll down | 1 — every visit (unless we cookie it) |
| SEO | Best — keywords **and** real content on `/` | `/` is thin marketing; content demoted a level |
| Returning readers | Land near content | Annoyed by the extra hop |
| Build effort | Moderate (just `app/page.tsx`) | Larger (move content to `/browse`, fix logo link, redirects, sitemap) |

The good news either way: a **big, bold hero** like Literotica's directly fixes what you didn't like about the small one I added — and I'll keep the `<h1>` + keywords intact for SEO.

Copy is evocative (not explicit) so it stays safe for previews, ad networks, and search snippets. --- ## PART 1 — HOMEPAGE COPY ### Hero # Lucifer's Diary ### Dark erotica, sex stories & adult fiction — confessions kept after dark A diary of the things people only whisper. Some entries are tender. Some are filthy. All of them are honest. Lucifer's Diary is a home for literary erotica and long-form sex stories written to be read slowly, after midnight. `[ Start Reading ]` `[ Browse by Tag ]` --- ### What this is This is my diary — the place I keep my darkest and most erotic fantasies. Every entry is something I actually wanted to write down: open-door and explicit, dark and filthy, or slow, deep, and romantic. They don't all live in the same mood, because neither do I. Every word here is mine. This isn't an anthology or a submission feed — it's one author, one voice, writing in their spare time, by hand. New pages go up when they're ready, so updates take a while. That's the point. Nothing here is churned out. This isn't a wall of throwaway smut. Each entry is adult fiction with craft behind it: sex stories that earn their heat, erotic series that take their time, and characters worth following into the dark. Every piece waited until it was worth confessing — and it's written to be read, not skimmed. --- ### Stories & series Standalone erotic tales for a single restless sitting, and multi-chapter slow-burn series for the nights you want the tension to build and build. Whether you came for a quick spicy read or a slow-burn erotic romance that unravels across dozens of chapters, you'll find adult short fiction here that treats desire as something worth writing well. ### Read anonymously No sign-up to start reading. Leave a like, save your place, pick up where you left off — an account is optional, never the price of admission. This site is anonymous by design: no tracking, no data harvesting, no name to hand over. Read like no one's watching, because no one is. ### Browse by tag Every story is tagged by theme and kink, so whatever you're in the mood for — soft and spicy or genuinely filthy, romantic or dark — the catalog bends to your taste. Filter by mood, length, heat level, and content so you always know what you're walking into. --- ### Erotica for people who love to read Lucifer's Diary is dark, literary erotica from a single author — adult fiction with real writing behind it. If you've been searching for free erotica online that doesn't read like everything else — sex stories with atmosphere, dark romance that takes its time, explicit short fiction that respects the reader — this is the diary you've been looking for. Pour a drink, dim the lights, and start reading. `[ Start Reading ]` --- ### Before you enter Lucifer's Diary contains explicit erotic fiction intended for adults only. By entering, you confirm you are 18 or older (21 where required) and that adult sexual content is legal to view where you are. All characters in every story are adults. `[ I'm 18+ — Let Me In ]` `[ Take Me Out ]` --- **Footer tagline:** *One author, after midnight. Dark, literary erotica — written to be read slowly.* --- --- ## PART 2 — SEO IMPLEMENTATION GUIDE ### 1. Title tag & meta description Place in the `` of the homepage. Title under ~60 characters, description under ~155. ```html Lucifer's Diary — Dark Erotica & Adult Sex Stories ``` ### 2. Heading hierarchy (critical) Search engines read structure. Use exactly **one** `

`, then `

` for each section. | Element | Content | |---|---| | `

` | Lucifer's Diary | | Subhead (`

Primary & secondary keywords These are already woven into the copy. Keep them in headings and the first 100 words. - **Primary:** dark erotica, sex stories, adult fiction, literary erotica - **Secondary:** slow-burn erotic series, dark romance, erotic short fiction, free erotica online - **Long-tail / low-competition (easiest to rank):** "erotica by a single author," "dark literary erotica," "slow-burn sex stories," "anonymous erotica no sign-up" Don't keyword-stuff. Each term should appear naturally; repetition beyond what's in the copy will hurt, not help. ### 4. Open Graph & Twitter cards (link previews) Controls how the site looks when shared. Use a non-explicit, on-brand preview image. ```html ``` ### 5. Adult-content & crawler signals Adult sites must self-label or they can be flagged/penalized. Internal links = the biggest homepage win A homepage with only static text ranks poorly. Add a **dynamic block of recent/featured story titles** with real links. This gives crawlers fresh content and fresh internal links every time you publish — the single highest-impact SEO move for a fiction site. ### 9. content.text:
Good catch. They're **two different components by design**, but their data overlaps in your situation, so they look identical:

| | "Pick up where you left off" | "Continue reading" |
|---|---|---|
| Source | **Backend** (`getContinueReading`) — scroll-position-driven, synced across devices | **localStorage** (client-only history) |
| Tracks | Exact page/% you were on (the "80%") | Which series you'd recently started |
| Works for | Logged-in users (needs session) | Everyone, including anonymous |

They were both added intentionally — one is the newer backend-synced resume, the other is the older localStorage history (which still helps anonymous readers). Trouble is: when a logged-in user has read just one chapter, **both rows point at that same chapter** — visually a duplicate, even though under the hood they're different signals.

### How to fix it (three options, smallest → biggest)

1. **Surgical dedup (Recommended).** Keep both rows, but hide any entry in "Continue reading" whose chapter is already shown in "Pick up where you left off." Result: duplicates vanish, but if the localStorage row has *extra* series the backend doesn't know about, you still see those. Best of both behaviors with the least UX change.

2. **Hide "Continue reading" entirely when "Pick up where you left off" has data.** Simpler; risks hiding localStorage-only series that aren't in the backend resume yet.

3. **Merge into a single "Continue reading" row** that prefers backend per-page resume and falls back to localStorage — one canonical row, no duplication possible. Cleaner design, but a bigger change (more code touched, harder to roll back).

### My recommendation
**Go with #1.** It's the cleanest fix that respects the existing design intent (both data sources still inform what you see) and removes the duplication you're seeing without risking lost information for edge cases. It's also the easiest to revert if you decide later you'd rather merge them.

Want me to ship #1, or would you rather go straight to #3 (the merge)? Either way I'll branch off `develop`, sandbox-test, PR, and merge — and you'll review on dev before promotion.

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

# UI/UX Pro Max - Design Intelligence

Comprehensive design guide for web and mobile applications. Contains 50+ styles, 161 color palettes, 57 font pairings, 161 product types with reasoning rules, 99 UX guidelines, and 25 chart types across 10 technology stacks. Searchable database with priority-based recommendations.

## When to Apply

This Skill should be used when the task involves **UI structure, visual design decisions, interaction patterns, or user experience quality control**.

### Must Use

This Skill must be invoked in the following situations:

- Designing new pages (Landing Page, Dashboard, Admin, SaaS, Mobile App)
- Creating or refactoring UI components (buttons, modals, forms, tables, charts, etc.)
- Choosing color schemes, typography systems, spacing standards, or layout systems
- Reviewing UI code for user experience, accessibility, or visual consistency
- Implementing navigation structures, animations, or responsive behavior
- Making product-level design decisions (style, information hierarchy, brand expression)
- Improving perceived quality, clarity, or usability of interfaces

### Recommended

This Skill is recommended in the following situations:

- UI looks "not professional enough" but the reason is unclear
- Receiving feedback on usability or experience
- Pre-launch UI quality optimization
- Aligning cross-platform design (Web / iOS / Android)
- Building design systems or reusable component libraries

### Skip

This Skill is not needed in the following situations:

- Pure backend logic development
- Only involving API or database design
- Performance optimization unrelated to the interface
- Infrastructure or DevOps work
- Non-visual scripts or automation tasks

**Decision criteria**: If the task will change how a feature **looks, feels, moves, or is interacted with**, this Skill should be used.

## Rule Categories by Priority

*For human/AI reference: follow priority 1→10 to decide which rule category to focus on first; use `--domain <Domain>` to query details when needed. Scripts do not read this table.*

| Priority | Category | Impact | Domain | Key Checks (Must Have) | Anti-Patterns (Avoid) |
|----------|----------|--------|--------|------------------------|------------------------|
| 1 | Accessibility | CRITICAL | `ux` | Contrast 4.5:1, Alt text, Keyboard nav, Aria-labels | Removing focus rings, Icon-only buttons without labels |
| 2 | Touch & Interaction | CRITICAL | `ux` | Min size 44×44px, 8px+ spacing, Loading feedback | Reliance on hover only, Instant state changes (0ms) |
| 3 | Performance | HIGH | `ux` | WebP/AVIF, Lazy loading, Reserve space (CLS < 0.1) | Layout thrashing, Cumulative Layout Shift |
| 4 | Style Selection | HIGH | `style`, `product` | Match product type, Consistency, SVG icons (no emoji) | Mixing flat & skeuomorphic randomly, Emoji as icons |
| 5 | Layout & Responsive | HIGH | `ux` | Mobile-first breakpoints, Viewport meta, No horizontal scroll | Horizontal scroll, Fixed px container widths, Disable zoom |
| 6 | Typography & Color | MEDIUM | `typography`, `color` | Base 16px, Line-height 1.5, Semantic color tokens | Text < 12px body, Gray-on-gray, Raw hex in components |
| 7 | Animation | MEDIUM | `ux` | Duration 150–300ms, Motion conveys meaning, Spatial continuity | Decorative-only animation, Animating width/height, No reduced-motion |
| 8 | Forms & Feedback | MEDIUM | `ux` | Visible labels, Error near field, Helper text, Progressive disclosure | Placeholder-only label, Errors only at top, Overwhelm upfront |
| 9 | Navigation Patterns | HIGH | `ux` | Predictable back, Bottom nav ≤5, Deep linking | Overloaded nav, Broken back behavior, No deep links |
| 10 | Charts & Data | LOW | `chart` | Legends, Tooltips, Accessible colors | Relying on color alone to convey meaning |

## Quick Reference

### 1. Accessibility (CRITICAL)

- `color-contrast` - Minimum 4.5:1 ratio for normal text (large text 3:1); Material Design
- `focus-states` - Visible focus rings on interactive elements (2–4px; Apple HIG, MD)
- `alt-text` - Descriptive alt text for meaningful images
- `aria-labels` - aria-label for icon-only buttons; accessibilityLabel in native (Apple HIG)
- `keyboard-nav` - Tab order matches visual order; full keyboard support (Apple HIG)
- `form-labels` - Use label with for attribute
- `skip-links` - Skip to main content for keyboard users
- `heading-hierarchy` - Sequential h1→h6, no level skip
- `color-not-only` - Don't convey info by color alone (add icon/text)
- `dynamic-type` - Support system text scaling; avoid truncation as text grows (Apple Dynamic Type, MD)
- `reduced-motion` - Respect prefers-reduced-motion; reduce/disable animations when requested (Apple Reduced Motion API, MD)
- `voiceover-sr` - Meaningful accessibilityLabel/accessibilityHint; logical reading order for VoiceOver/screen readers (Apple HIG, MD)
- `escape-routes` - Provide cancel/back in modals and multi-step flows (Apple HIG)
- `keyboard-shortcuts` - Preserve system and a11y shortcuts; offer keyboard alternatives for drag-and-drop (Apple HIG)

### 2. Touch & Interaction (CRITICAL)

- `touch-target-size` - Min 44×44pt (Apple) / 48×48dp (Material); extend hit area beyond visual bounds if needed
- `touch-spacing` - Minimum 8px/8dp gap between touch targets (Apple HIG, MD)
- `hover-vs-tap` - Use click/tap for primary interactions; don't rely on hover alone
- `loading-buttons` - Disable button during async operations; show spinner or progress
- `error-feedback` - Clear error messages near problem
- `cursor-pointer` - Add cursor-pointer to clickable elements (Web)
- `gesture-conflicts` - Avoid horizontal swipe on main content; prefer vertical scroll
- `tap-delay` - Use touch-action: manipulation to reduce 300ms delay (Web)
- `standard-gestures` - Use platform standard gestures consistently; don't redefine (e.g. swipe-back, pinch-zoom) (Apple HIG)
- `system-gestures` - Don't block system gestures (Control Center, back swipe, etc.) (Apple HIG)
- `press-feedback` - Visual feedback on press (ripple/highlight; MD state layers)
- `haptic-feedback` - Use haptic for confirmations and important actions; avoid overuse (Apple HIG)
- `gesture-alternative` - Don't rely on gesture-only interactions; always provide visible controls for critical actions
- `safe-area-awareness` - Keep primary touch targets away from notch, Dynamic Island, gesture bar and screen edges
- `no-precision-required` - Avoid requiring pixel-perfect taps on small icons or thin edges
- `swipe-clarity` - Swipe actions must show clear affordance or hint (chevron, label, tutorial)
- `drag-threshold` - Use a movement threshold before starting drag to avoid accidental drags

### 3. Performance (HIGH)

- `image-optimization` - Use WebP/AVIF, responsive images (srcset/sizes), lazy load non-critical assets
- `image-dimension` - Declare width/height or use aspect-ratio to prevent layout shift (Core Web Vitals: CLS)
- `font-loading` - Use font-display: swap/optional to avoid invisible text (FOIT); reserve space to reduce layout shift (MD)
- `font-preload` - Preload only critical fonts; avoid overusing preload on every variant
- `critical-css` - Prioritize above-the-fold CSS (inline critical CSS or early-loaded stylesheet)
- `lazy-loading` - Lazy load non-hero components via dynamic import / route-level splitting
- `bundle-splitting` - Split code by route/feature (React Suspense / Next.js dynamic) to reduce initial load and TTI
- `third-party-scripts` - Load third-party scripts async/defer; audit and remove unnecessary ones (MD)
- `reduce-reflows` - Avoid frequent layout reads/writes; batch DOM reads then writes
- `content-jumping` - Reserve space for async content to avoid layout jumps (Core Web Vitals: CLS)
- `lazy-load-below-fold` - Use loading="lazy" for below-the-fold images and heavy media
- `virtualize-lists` - Virtualize lists with 50+ items to improve memory efficiency and scroll performance
- `main-thread-budget` - Keep per-frame work under ~16ms for 60fps; move heavy tasks off main thread (HIG, MD)
- `progressive-loading` - Use skeleton screens / shimmer instead of long blocking spinners for >1s operations (Apple HIG)
- `input-latency` - Keep input latency under ~100ms for taps/scrolls (Material responsiveness standard)
- `tap-feedback-speed` - Provide visual feedback within 100ms of tap (Apple HIG)
- `debounce-throttle` - Use debounce/throttle for high-frequency events (scroll, resize, input)
- `offline-support` - Provide offline state messaging and basic fallback (PWA / mobile)
- `network-fallback` - Offer degraded modes for slow networks (lower-res images, fewer animations)

### 4. Style Selection (HIGH)

- `style-match` - Match style to product type (use `--design-system` for recommendations)
- `consistency` - Use same style across all pages
- `no-emoji-icons` - Use SVG icons (Heroicons, Lucide), not emojis
- `color-palette-from-product` - Choose palette from product/industry (search `--domain color`)
- `effects-match-style` - Shadows, blur, radius aligned with chosen style (glass / flat / clay etc.)
- `platform-adaptive` - Respect platform idioms (iOS HIG vs Material): navigation, controls, typography, motion
- `state-clarity` - Make hover/pressed/disabled states visually distinct while staying on-style (Material state layers)
- `elevation-consistent` - Use a consistent elevation/shadow scale for cards, sheets, modals; avoid random shadow values
- `dark-mode-pairing` - Design light/dark variants together to keep brand, contrast, and style consistent
- `icon-style-consistent` - Use one icon set/visual language (stroke width, corner radius) across the product
- `system-controls` - Prefer native/system controls over fully custom ones; only customize when branding requires it (Apple HIG)
- `blur-purpose` - Use blur to indicate background dismissal (modals, sheets), not as decoration (Apple HIG)
- `primary-action` - Each screen should have only one primary CTA; secondary actions visually subordinate (Apple HIG)

### 5. Layout & Responsive (HIGH)

- `viewport-meta` - width=device-width initial-scale=1 (never disable zoom)
- `mobile-first` - Design mobile-first, then scale up to tablet and desktop
- `breakpoint-consistency` - Use systematic breakpoints (e.g. 375 / 768 / 1024 / 1440)
- `readable-font-size` - Minimum 16px body text on mobile (avoids iOS auto-zoom)
- `line-length-control` - Mobile 35–60 chars per line; desktop 60–75 chars
- `horizontal-scroll` - No horizontal scroll on mobile; ensure content fits viewport width
- `spacing-scale` - Use 4pt/8dp incremental spacing system (Material Design)
- `touch-density` - Keep component spacing comfortable for touch: not cramped, not causing mis-taps
- `container-width` - Consistent max-width on desktop (max-w-6xl / 7xl)
- `z-index-management` - Define layered z-index scale (e.g. 0 / 10 / 20 / 40 / 100 / 1000)
- `fixed-element-offset` - Fixed navbar/bottom bar must reserve safe padding for underlying content
- `scroll-behavior` - Avoid nested scroll regions that interfere with the main scroll experience
- `viewport-units` - Prefer min-h-dvh over 100vh on mobile
- `orientation-support` - Keep layout readable and operable in landscape mode
- `content-priority` - Show core content first on mobile; fold or hide secondary content
- `visual-hierarchy` - Establish hierarchy via size, spacing, contrast — not color alone

### 6. Typography & Color (MEDIUM)

- `line-height` - Use 1.5-1.75 for body text
- `line-length` - Limit to 65-75 characters per line
- `font-pairing` - Match heading/body font personalities
- `font-scale` - Consistent type scale (e.g. 12 14 16 18 24 32)
- `contrast-readability` - Darker text on light backgrounds (e.g. slate-900 on white)
- `text-styles-system` - Use platform type system: iOS 11 Dynamic Type styles / Material 5 type roles (display, headline, title, body, label) (HIG, MD)
- `weight-hierarchy` - Use font-weight to reinforce hierarchy: Bold headings (600–700), Regular body (400), Medium labels (500) (MD)
- `color-semantic` - Define semantic color tokens (primary, secondary, error, surface, on-surface) not raw hex in components (Material color system)
- `color-dark-mode` - Dark mode uses desaturated / lighter tonal variants, not inverted colors; test contrast separately (HIG, MD)
- `color-accessible-pairs` - Foreground/background pairs must meet 4.5:1 (AA) or 7:1 (AAA); use tools to verify (WCAG, MD)
- `color-not-decorative-only` - Functional color (error red, success green) must include icon/text; avoid color-only meaning (HIG, MD)
- `truncation-strategy` - Prefer wrapping over truncation; when truncating use ellipsis and provide full text via tooltip/expand (Apple HIG)
- `letter-spacing` - Respect default letter-spacing per platform; avoid tight tracking on body text (HIG, MD)
- `number-tabular` - Use tabular/monospaced figures for data columns, prices, and timers to prevent layout shift
- `whitespace-balance` - Use whitespace intentionally to group related items and separate sections; avoid visual clutter (Apple HIG)

### 7. Animation (MEDIUM)

- `duration-timing` - Use 150–300ms for micro-interactions; complex transitions ≤400ms; avoid >500ms (MD)
- `transform-performance` - Use transform/opacity only; avoid animating width/height/top/left
- `loading-states` - Show skeleton or progress indicator when loading exceeds 300ms
- `excessive-motion` - Animate 1-2 key elements per view max
- `easing` - Use ease-out for entering, ease-in for exiting; avoid linear for UI transitions
- `motion-meaning` - Every animation must express a cause-effect relationship, not just be decorative (Apple HIG)
- `state-transition` - State changes (hover / active / expanded / collapsed / modal) should animate smoothly, not snap
- `continuity` - Page/screen transitions should maintain spatial continuity (shared element, directional slide) (Apple HIG)
- `parallax-subtle` - Use parallax sparingly; must respect reduced-motion and not cause disorientation (Apple HIG)
- `spring-physics` - Prefer spring/physics-based curves over linear or cubic-bezier for natural feel (Apple HIG fluid animations)
- `exit-faster-than-enter` - Exit animations shorter than enter (~60–70% of enter duration) to feel responsive (MD motion)
- `stagger-sequence` - Stagger list/grid item entrance by 30–50ms per item; avoid all-at-once or too-slow reveals (MD)
- `shared-element-transition` - Use shared element / hero transitions for visual continuity between screens (MD, HIG)
- `interruptible` - Animations must be interruptible; user tap/gesture cancels in-progress animation immediately (Apple HIG)
- `no-blocking-animation` - Never block user input during an animation; UI must stay interactive (Apple HIG)
- `fade-crossfade` - Use crossfade for content replacement within the same container (MD)
- `scale-feedback` - Subtle scale (0.95–1.05) on press for tappable cards/buttons; restore on release (HIG, MD)
- `gesture-feedback` - Drag, swipe, and pinch must provide real-time visual response tracking the finger (MD Motion)
- `hierarchy-motion` - Use translate/scale direction to express hierarchy: enter from below = deeper, exit upward = back (MD)
- `motion-consistency` - Unify duration/easing tokens globally; all animations share the same rhythm and feel
- `opacity-threshold` - Fading elements should not linger below opacity 0.2; either fade fully or remain visible
- `modal-motion` - Modals/sheets should animate from their trigger source (scale+fade or slide-in) for spatial context (HIG, MD)
- `navigation-direction` - Forward navigation animates left/up; backward animates right/down — keep direction logically consistent (HIG)
- `layout-shift-avoid` - Animations must not cause layout reflow or CLS; use transform for position changes

### 8. Forms & Feedback (MEDIUM)

- `input-labels` - Visible label per input (not placeholder-only)
- `error-placement` - Show error below the related field
- `submit-feedback` - Loading then success/error state on submit
- `required-indicators` - Mark required fields (e.g. asterisk)
- `empty-states` - Helpful message and action when no content
- `toast-dismiss` - Auto-dismiss toasts in 3-5s
- `confirmation-dialogs` - Confirm before destructive actions
- `input-helper-text` - Provide persistent helper text below complex inputs, not just placeholder (Material Design)
- `disabled-states` - Disabled elements use reduced opacity (0.38–0.5) + cursor change + semantic attribute (MD)
- `progressive-disclosure` - Reveal complex options progressively; don't overwhelm users upfront (Apple HIG)
- `inline-validation` - Validate on blur (not keystroke); show error only after user finishes input (MD)
- `input-type-keyboard` - Use semantic input types (email, tel, number) to trigger the correct mobile keyboard (HIG, MD)
- `password-toggle` - Provide show/hide toggle for password fields (MD)
- `autofill-support` - Use autocomplete / textContentType attributes so the system can autofill (HIG, MD)
- `undo-support` - Allow undo for destructive or bulk actions (e.g. "Undo delete" toast) (Apple HIG)
- `success-feedback` - Confirm completed actions with brief visual feedback (checkmark, toast, color flash) (MD)
- `error-recovery` - Error messages must include a clear recovery path (retry, edit, help link) (HIG, MD)
- `multi-step-progress` - Multi-step flows show step indicator or progress bar; allow back navigation (MD)
- `form-autosave` - Long forms should auto-save drafts to prevent data loss on accidental dismissal (Apple HIG)
- `sheet-dismiss-confirm` - Confirm before dismissing a sheet/modal with unsaved changes (Apple HIG)
- `error-clarity` - Error messages must state cause + how to fix (not just "Invalid input") (HIG, MD)
- `field-grouping` - Group related fields logically (fieldset/legend or visual grouping) (MD)
- `read-only-distinction` - Read-only state should be visually and semantically different from disabled (MD)
- `focus-management` - After submit error, auto-focus the first invalid field (WCAG, MD)
- `error-summary` - For multiple errors, show summary at top with anchor links to each field (WCAG)
- `touch-friendly-input` - Mobile input height ≥44px to meet touch target requirements (Apple HIG)
- `destructive-emphasis` - Destructive actions use semantic danger color (red) and are visually separated from primary actions (HIG, MD)
- `toast-accessibility` - Toasts must not steal focus; use aria-live="polite" for screen reader announcement (WCAG)
- `aria-live-errors` - Form errors use aria-live region or role="alert" to notify screen readers (WCAG)
- `contrast-feedback` - Error and success state colors must meet 4.5:1 contrast ratio (WCAG, MD)
- `timeout-feedback` - Request timeout must show clear feedback with retry option (MD)

### 9. Navigation Patterns (HIGH)

- `bottom-nav-limit` - Bottom navigation max 5 items; use labels with icons (Material Design)
- `drawer-usage` - Use drawer/sidebar for secondary navigation, not primary actions (Material Design)
- `back-behavior` - Back navigation must be predictable and consistent; preserve scroll/state (Apple HIG, MD)
- `deep-linking` - All key screens must be reachable via deep link / URL for sharing and notifications (Apple HIG, MD)
- `tab-bar-ios` - iOS: use bottom Tab Bar for top-level navigation (Apple HIG)
- `top-app-bar-android` - Android: use Top App Bar with navigation icon for primary structure (Material Design)
- `nav-label-icon` - Navigation items must have both icon and text label; icon-only nav harms discoverability (MD)
- `nav-state-active` - Current location must be visually highlighted (color, weight, indicator) in navigation (HIG, MD)
- `nav-hierarchy` - Primary nav (tabs/bottom bar) vs secondary nav (drawer/settings) must be clearly separated (MD)
- `modal-escape` - Modals and sheets must offer a clear close/dismiss affordance; swipe-down to dismiss on mobile (Apple HIG)
- `search-accessible` - Search must be easily reachable (top bar or tab); provide recent/suggested queries (MD)
- `breadcrumb-web` - Web: use breadcrumbs for 3+ level deep hierarchies to aid orientation (MD)
- `state-preservation` - Navigating back must restore previous scroll position, filter state, and input (HIG, MD)
- `gesture-nav-support` - Support system gesture navigation (iOS swipe-back, Android predictive back) without conflict (HIG, MD)
- `tab-badge` - Use badges on nav items sparingly to indicate unread/pending; clear after user visits (HIG, MD)
- `overflow-menu` - When actions exceed available space, use overflow/more menu instead of cramming (MD)
- `bottom-nav-top-level` - Bottom nav is for top-level screens only; never nest sub-navigation inside it (MD)
- `adaptive-navigation` - Large screens (≥1024px) prefer sidebar; small screens use bottom/top nav (Material Adaptive)
- `back-stack-integrity` - Never silently reset the navigation stack or unexpectedly jump to home (HIG, MD)
- `navigation-consistency` - Navigation placement must stay the same across all pages; don't change by page type
- `avoid-mixed-patterns` - Don't mix Tab + Sidebar + Bottom Nav at the same hierarchy level
- `modal-vs-navigation` - Modals must not be used for primary navigation flows; they break the user's path (HIG)
- `focus-on-route-change` - After page transition, move focus to main content region for screen reader users (WCAG)
- `persistent-nav` - Core navigation must remain reachable from deep pages; don't hide it entirely in sub-flows (HIG, MD)
- `destructive-nav-separation` - Dangerous actions (delete account, logout) must be visually and spatially separated from normal nav items (HIG, MD)
- `empty-nav-state` - When a nav destination is unavailable, explain why instead of silently hiding it (MD)

### 10. Charts & Data (LOW)

- `chart-type` - Match chart type to data type (trend → line, comparison → bar, proportion → pie/donut)
- `color-guidance` - Use accessible color palettes; avoid red/green only pairs for colorblind users (WCAG, MD)
- `data-table` - Provide table alternative for accessibility; charts alone are not screen-reader friendly (WCAG)
- `pattern-texture` - Supplement color with patterns, textures, or shapes so data is distinguishable without color (WCAG, MD)
- `legend-visible` - Always show legend; position near the chart, not detached below a scroll fold (MD)
- `tooltip-on-interact` - Provide tooltips/data labels on hover (Web) or tap (mobile) showing exact values (HIG, MD)
- `axis-labels` - Label axes with units and readable scale; avoid truncated or rotated labels on mobile
- `responsive-chart` - Charts must reflow or simplify on small screens (e.g. horizontal bar instead of vertical, fewer ticks)
- `empty-data-state` - Show meaningful empty state when no data exists ("No data yet" + guidance), not a blank chart (MD)
- `loading-chart` - Use skeleton or shimmer placeholder while chart data loads; don't show an empty axis frame
- `animation-optional` - Chart entrance animations must respect prefers-reduced-motion; data should be readable immediately (HIG)
- `large-dataset` - For 1000+ data points, aggregate or sample; provide drill-down for detail instead of rendering all (MD)
- `number-formatting` - Use locale-aware formatting for numbers, dates, currencies on axes and labels (HIG, MD)
- `touch-target-chart` - Interactive chart elements (points, segments) must have ≥44pt tap area or expand on touch (Apple HIG)
- `no-pie-overuse` - Avoid pie/donut for >5 categories; switch to bar chart for clarity
- `contrast-data` - Data lines/bars vs background ≥3:1; data text labels ≥4.5:1 (WCAG)
- `legend-interactive` - Legends should be clickable to toggle series visibility (MD)
- `direct-labeling` - For small datasets, label values directly on the chart to reduce eye travel
- `tooltip-keyboard` - Tooltip content must be keyboard-reachable and not rely on hover alone (WCAG)
- `sortable-table` - Data tables must support sorting with aria-sort indicating current sort state (WCAG)
- `axis-readability` - Axis ticks must not be cramped; maintain readable spacing, auto-skip on small screens
- `data-density` - Limit information density per chart to avoid cognitive overload; split into multiple charts if needed
- `trend-emphasis` - Emphasize data trends over decoration; avoid heavy gradients/shadows that obscure the data
- `gridline-subtle` - Grid lines should be low-contrast (e.g. gray-200) so they don't compete with data
- `focusable-elements` - Interactive chart elements (points, bars, slices) must be keyboard-navigable (WCAG)
- `screen-reader-summary` - Provide a text summary or aria-label describing the chart's key insight for screen readers (WCAG)
- `error-state-chart` - Data load failure must show error message with retry action, not a broken/empty chart
- `export-option` - For data-heavy products, offer CSV/image export of chart data
- `drill-down-consistency` - Drill-down interactions must maintain a clear back-path and hierarchy breadcrumb
- `time-scale-clarity` - Time series charts must clearly label time granularity (day/week/month) and allow switching

## Common Rules for Professional UI

These are frequently overlooked issues that make UI look unprofessional:
Scope notice: The rules below are for App UI (iOS/Android/React Native/Flutter), not desktop-web interaction patterns.

### Icons & Visual Elements

| Rule | Standard | Avoid | Why It Matters |
|------|----------|--------|----------------|
| **No Emoji as Structural Icons** | Use vector-based icons (e.g., Lucide, react-native-vector-icons, @expo/vector-icons). | Using emojis (🎨 🚀 ⚙️) for navigation, settings, or system controls. | Emojis are font-dependent, inconsistent across platforms, and cannot be controlled via design tokens. |
| **Vector-Only Assets** | Use SVG or platform vector icons that scale cleanly and support theming. | Raster PNG icons that blur or pixelate. | Ensures scalability, crisp rendering, and dark/light mode adaptability. |
| **Stable Interaction States** | Use color, opacity, or elevation transitions for press states without changing layout bounds. | Layout-shifting transforms that move surrounding content or trigger visual jitter. | Prevents unstable interactions and preserves smooth motion/perceived quality on mobile. |
| **Correct Brand Logos** | Use official brand assets and follow their usage guidelines (spacing, color, clear space). | Guessing logo paths, recoloring unofficially, or modifying proportions. | Prevents brand misuse and ensures legal/platform compliance. |
| **Consistent Icon Sizing** | Define icon sizes as design tokens (e.g., icon-sm, icon-md = 24pt, icon-lg). | Mixing arbitrary values like 20pt / 24pt / 28pt randomly. | Maintains rhythm and visual hierarchy across the interface. |
| **Stroke Consistency** | Use a consistent stroke width within the same visual layer (e.g., 1.5px or 2px). | Mixing thick and thin stroke styles arbitrarily. | Inconsistent strokes reduce perceived polish and cohesion. |
| **Filled vs Outline Discipline** | Use one icon style per hierarchy level. | Mixing filled and outline icons at the same hierarchy level. | Maintains semantic clarity and stylistic coherence. |
| **Touch Target Minimum** | Minimum 44×44pt interactive area (use hitSlop if icon is smaller). | Small icons without expanded tap area. | Meets accessibility and platform usability standards. |
| **Icon Alignment** | Align icons to text baseline and maintain consistent padding. | Misaligned icons or inconsistent spacing around them. | Prevents subtle visual imbalance that reduces perceived quality. |
| **Icon Contrast** | Follow WCAG contrast standards: 4.5:1 for small elements, 3:1 minimum for larger UI glyphs. | Low-contrast icons that blend into the background. | Ensures accessibility in both light and dark modes. |


### Interaction (App)

| Rule | Do | Don't |
|------|----|----- |
| **Tap feedback** | Provide clear pressed feedback (ripple/opacity/elevation) within 80-150ms | No visual response on tap |
| **Animation timing** | Keep micro-interactions around 150-300ms with platform-native easing | Instant transitions or slow animations (>500ms) |
| **Accessibility focus** | Ensure screen reader focus order matches visual order and labels are descriptive | Unlabeled controls or confusing focus traversal |
| **Disabled state clarity** | Use disabled semantics (`disabled`/native disabled props), reduced emphasis, and no tap action | Controls that look tappable but do nothing |
| **Touch target minimum** | Keep tap areas >=44x44pt (iOS) or >=48x48dp (Android), expand hit area when icon is smaller | Tiny tap targets or icon-only hit areas without padding |
| **Gesture conflict prevention** | Keep one primary gesture per region and avoid nested tap/drag conflicts | Overlapping gestures causing accidental actions |
| **Semantic native controls** | Prefer native interactive primitives (`Button`, `Pressable`, platform equivalents) with proper accessibility roles | Generic containers used as primary controls without semantics |

### Light/Dark Mode Contrast

| Rule | Do | Don't |
|------|----|----- |
| **Surface readability (light)** | Keep cards/surfaces clearly separated from background with sufficient opacity/elevation | Overly transparent surfaces that blur hierarchy |
| **Text contrast (light)** | Maintain body text contrast >=4.5:1 against light surfaces | Low-contrast gray body text |
| **Text contrast (dark)** | Maintain primary text contrast >=4.5:1 and secondary text >=3:1 on dark surfaces | Dark mode text that blends into background |
| **Border and divider visibility** | Ensure separators are visible in both themes (not just light mode) | Theme-specific borders disappearing in one mode |
| **State contrast parity** | Keep pressed/focused/disabled states equally distinguishable in light and dark themes | Defining interaction states for one theme only |
| **Token-driven theming** | Use semantic color tokens mapped per theme across app surfaces/text/icons | Hardcoded per-screen hex values |
| **Scrim and modal legibility** | Use a modal scrim strong enough to isolate foreground content (typically 40-60% black) | Weak scrim that leaves background visually competing |

### Layout & Spacing

| Rule | Do | Don't |
|------|----|----- |
| **Safe-area compliance** | Respect top/bottom safe areas for all fixed headers, tab bars, and CTA bars | Placing fixed UI under notch, status bar, or gesture area |
| **System bar clearance** | Add spacing for status/navigation bars and gesture home indicator | Let tappable content collide with OS chrome |
| **Consistent content width** | Keep predictable content width per device class (phone/tablet) | Mixing arbitrary widths between screens |
| **8dp spacing rhythm** | Use a consistent 4/8dp spacing system for padding/gaps/section spacing | Random spacing increments with no rhythm |
| **Readable text measure** | Keep long-form text readable on large devices (avoid edge-to-edge paragraphs on tablets) | Full-width long text that hurts readability |
| **Section spacing hierarchy** | Define clear vertical rhythm tiers (e.g., 16/24/32/48) by hierarchy | Similar UI levels with inconsistent spacing |
| **Adaptive gutters by breakpoint** | Increase horizontal insets on larger widths and in landscape | Same narrow gutter on all device sizes/orientations |
| **Scroll and fixed element coexistence** | Add bottom/top content insets so lists are not hidden behind fixed bars | Scroll content obscured by sticky headers/footers |

## Pre-Delivery Checklist

Before delivering UI code, verify these items:
Scope notice: This checklist is for App UI (iOS/Android/React Native/Flutter).

### Visual Quality
- [ ] No emojis used as icons (use SVG instead)
- [ ] All icons come from a consistent icon family and style
- [ ] Official brand assets are used with correct proportions and clear space
- [ ] Pressed-state visuals do not shift layout bounds or cause jitter

- [ ] All tappable elements provide clear pressed feedback (ripple/opacity/elevation)
- [ ] Touch targets meet minimum size (>=44x44pt iOS, >=48x48dp Android)
- [ ] Micro-interaction timing stays in the 150-300ms range with native-feeling easing
- [ ] Disabled states are visually clear and non-interactive
- [ ] Screen reader focus order matches visual order, and interactive labels are descriptive
- [ ] Gesture regions avoid nested/conflicting interactions (tap/drag/back-swipe conflicts)

### Light/Dark Mode
- [ ] Primary text contrast >=4.5:1 in both light and dark mode
- [ ] Secondary text contrast >=3:1 in both light and dark mode
- [ ] Dividers/borders and interaction states are distinguishable in both modes
- [ ] Modal/drawer scrim opacity is strong enough to preserve foreground legibility (typically 40-60% black)
- [ ] Both themes are tested before delivery (not inferred from a single theme)

### Layout
- [ ] Safe areas are respected for headers, tab bars, and bottom CTA bars
- [ ] Scroll content is not hidden behind fixed/sticky bars
- [ ] Verified on small phone, large phone, and tablet (portrait + landscape)
- [ ] Horizontal insets/gutters adapt correctly by device size and orientation
- [ ] 4/8dp spacing rhythm is maintained across component, section, and page levels
- [ ] Long-form text measure remains readable on larger devices (no edge-to-edge paragraphs)

### Accessibility
- [ ] All meaningful images/icons have accessibility labels
- [ ] Form fields have labels, hints, and clear error messages
- [ ] Color is not the only indicator
- [ ] Reduced motion and dynamic text size are supported without layout breakage

content.text:
Got the framework. Here's the consolidated plan based on the PDF + the design rules. Read through and tell me what to adjust — I won't write code until you sign off.

## What I'll build

**Replace the slide-out NotesDrawer entirely.** In the admin story/chapter editor, the empty right column becomes a **persistent Notes panel** containing a vertical list of *many* notes (not one big textarea), with an **+ Add note** button at the bottom.

Each note has two visual states:

| State | What you see |
|---|---|
| **Collapsed pill** (default) | Tiny color dot · title (truncated) · 3-dot menu — one short row |
| **Expanded card** (click pill) | Title input + multi-line body + 3-dot menu — expands inline, in place |

3-dot menu on each note: **Change color · Delete** (with undo toast).

## Color palette (suggestion)
Six colors that work on the dark canvas — five accents + a neutral:

1. **Gold** (default — brand) 2. **Crimson** 3. **Sage** 4. **Indigo** 5. **Amber** 6. **Slate** (neutral / "no color")

Per a11y: each color has a visible name in the menu + an `aria-label` so color isn't the only signal; the title text always carries the note's meaning.

## What this actually touches (honest scope)
This isn't a UI-only change — `notes` today is a single `string` field on `Story` and `Chapter`. To support many color-coded notes I need:

| Layer | Work |
|---|---|
| **Backend** (NestJS + Prisma) | New `Note` model (`id, storyId?/chapterId?, title, body, color, order, …`), Notes module (controller/service/DTOs), Prisma migration, **data migration** for existing `notes` strings |
| **Frontend** | `NotesPanel` (the right column), `NoteCard` (collapsed/expanded), color-picker popover, undo toast, autosave per note. Remove the old NotesDrawer trigger. Editor page becomes a 2-column layout |

Recommended sequencing: **2 PRs** (backend first, then frontend) — frontend can develop against the merged API.

## MVP discipline (what I'll deliberately defer to v2)
- Drag-to-reorder (manual order can come later — for v1 use created-date order)
- Rich text inside note bodies (plain `<textarea>` for v1)
- Per-color filtering / search / pinning
- Cross-device sync of "which note is currently expanded"

## Six decisions I need from you before I start

1. **Color palette** — accept my 6 (Gold, Crimson, Sage, Indigo, Amber, Slate), or pick different / label them by purpose (Plot / Character / Theme / Setting / Voice / Other)?
2. **Body editor** — plain `<textarea>` (simple, MVP) or TipTap rich-text (matches editor style, more code)? I recommend plain for v1.
3. **One expanded at a time, or many?** — I recommend **one** (cleaner, focuses you on the note).
4. **Existing `notes` strings** — for stories/chapters that already have content in `notes`, I'll migrate it into one new note titled *"Note"* with the existing text + Gold color. OK?
5. **PR strategy** — two sequential PRs (backend → frontend), or one big PR?
6. **Mobile** — on narrow widths the right column won't fit beside the editor. Should it (a) stay as a floating button that opens a panel/sheet, or (b) move below the form as a stacked section? I lean (a) on mobile — your sketches were desktop-only, so this needs your call.

Tell me your picks (even just "all defaults") and I'll branch off `develop` and start.

-- =====================================================================
-- Add multi-card, color-coded admin Notes — replaces the single
-- `notes` string column previously on `stories` and `chapters`.
--
-- Steps (must run in this order, single transaction):
--   1. Create the NoteColor enum.
--   2. Create the `notes` table + indexes + FK constraints.
--   3. Add the polymorphic-owner XOR CHECK constraint.
--   4. Backfill: one row per Story/Chapter that has non-empty
--      legacy notes content — title 'Note', color GOLD, orderIndex 0.
--   5. Drop the legacy `stories.notes` and `chapters.notes` columns.
--
-- Postgres 16 is required (gen_random_uuid() is built-in, no
-- pgcrypto extension needed).
-- =====================================================================

-- 1. Enum --------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TYPE "NoteColor" AS ENUM ('GOLD', 'CRIMSON', 'SAGE', 'INDIGO', 'AMBER', 'SLATE');

-- 2. Table + indexes ---------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE "notes" (
    "id"          TEXT        NOT NULL,
    "story_id"    TEXT,
    "chapter_id"  TEXT,
    "title"       TEXT        NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    "body"        TEXT        NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    "color"       "NoteColor" NOT NULL DEFAULT 'GOLD',
    "order_index" INTEGER     NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    "created_at"  TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    "updated_at"  TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL,

    CONSTRAINT "notes_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("id")
);

CREATE INDEX "notes_story_id_order_index_idx"
    ON "notes" ("story_id", "order_index");
CREATE INDEX "notes_chapter_id_order_index_idx"
    ON "notes" ("chapter_id", "order_index");

ALTER TABLE "notes"
    ADD CONSTRAINT "notes_story_id_fkey"
    FOREIGN KEY ("story_id") REFERENCES "stories"("id")
    ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE;

ALTER TABLE "notes"
    ADD CONSTRAINT "notes_chapter_id_fkey"
    FOREIGN KEY ("chapter_id") REFERENCES "chapters"("id")
    ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE;

-- 3. Polymorphic owner — exactly one of (story_id, chapter_id) ---------
-- Prisma can't express this; enforced here so the invariant survives
-- any future code path that tries to write a row with neither or both.
ALTER TABLE "notes"
    ADD CONSTRAINT "notes_owner_xor"
    CHECK (("story_id" IS NULL) <> ("chapter_id" IS NULL));

-- 4. Backfill from legacy `notes` columns ------------------------------
INSERT INTO "notes"
    ("id", "story_id", "title", "body", "color", "order_index", "created_at", "updated_at")
SELECT
    gen_random_uuid()::text,
    "id",
    'Note',
    "notes",
    'GOLD',
    0,
    NOW(),
    NOW()
FROM "stories"
WHERE "notes" IS NOT NULL AND TRIM("notes") <> '';

INSERT INTO "notes"
    ("id", "chapter_id", "title", "body", "color", "order_index", "created_at", "updated_at")
SELECT
    gen_random_uuid()::text,
    "id",
    'Note',
    "notes",
    'GOLD',
    0,
    NOW(),
    NOW()
FROM "chapters"
WHERE "notes" IS NOT NULL AND TRIM("notes") <> '';

-- 5. Drop the legacy single-string note columns ------------------------
ALTER TABLE "stories"  DROP COLUMN "notes";
ALTER TABLE "chapters" DROP COLUMN "notes";
