cd "/Users/taha/Claude projects/LucifersDiary" && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
feat(notes): multi-card color-coded admin notes — backend (model + API + migration)

Replaces the single legacy `notes` string on Story and Chapter with a
proper Note model so the admin can keep many colored note cards per
piece. Frontend PR follows.

Schema (backend/prisma/schema.prisma)
- New Note model: id, storyId? | chapterId? (polymorphic, XOR), title,
  body, color, orderIndex, timestamps. Cascade-delete from owner.
- New NoteColor enum: GOLD, CRIMSON, SAGE, INDIGO, AMBER, SLATE.
- Story.notes / Chapter.notes change from String? to Note[] relation.

Migration (20260608200000_add_notes_model/migration.sql)
- Creates the enum, table, indexes, FKs, and an `notes_owner_xor`
  CHECK so exactly one of (story_id, chapter_id) is set even outside
  Prisma's reach.
- Backfills one Note (title 'Note', color GOLD, orderIndex 0) for every
  Story/Chapter whose legacy `notes` string is non-empty, then drops the
  legacy columns. Postgres 16+ (gen_random_uuid()).

API (src/notes/, admin-only, JwtAuthGuard)
- GET    /admin/notes?storyId=... | ?chapterId=...   list
- POST   /admin/notes                                create
- PATCH  /admin/notes/:id                            update
- DELETE /admin/notes/:id                            delete
- Service enforces owner XOR + existence + soft-delete check, picks
  next orderIndex on create.

DTO cleanup
- create-story.dto.ts / create-chapter.dto.ts: drop the `notes` field.
  With `forbidNonWhitelisted: true` the API now 400s on `notes` in
  story/chapter bodies — the frontend PR will route note edits to
  /admin/notes instead.

Deployment note: this migration drops two columns after backfill —
fine because the values move into the notes table, but it means the
old frontend MUST NOT be deployed against this backend by itself.
Deploy backend + frontend together (or backend after both PRs are
merged to main).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3 && echo "=== push ===" && git push -u origin feat/notes-backend 2>&1 | tail -3

## Summary
Backend half of the admin notes redesign. Replaces the single-string `notes` column on `Story` and `Chapter` with a proper **`Note`** model so the admin can keep many **color-coded** note cards per piece. The frontend PR lands next; this one is API + schema only.

### Schema (`backend/prisma/schema.prisma`)
- New **`Note`** model: `id`, `storyId?` *or* `chapterId?` (polymorphic, XOR), `title`, `body`, `color`, `orderIndex`, timestamps. Cascade-delete from owner.
- New **`NoteColor`** enum: **GOLD · CRIMSON · SAGE · INDIGO · AMBER · SLATE** (your six).
- `Story.notes` / `Chapter.notes` switch from `String?` to **`Note[]`** relation.

### Migration (`20260608200000_add_notes_model/migration.sql`)
- Creates enum, `notes` table, indexes, FKs, and a **`notes_owner_xor` CHECK** so exactly one of `(story_id, chapter_id)` is set even outside Prisma's reach.
- **Backfills** one Note (title `'Note'`, color `GOLD`, orderIndex 0) for every Story/Chapter whose legacy `notes` string is non-empty (per your decision #4), then drops the legacy columns.
- Postgres 16+ (uses `gen_random_uuid()` natively, no extension needed — matches DEPLOY.md).

### API — admin only (`src/notes/`)
All behind `JwtAuthGuard`, registered in `app.module.ts`:

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET`    | `/admin/notes?storyId=…` *or* `?chapterId=…` | list owner's notes (ordered by `orderIndex`) |
| `POST`   | `/admin/notes` | create — body: `{ storyId?\|chapterId?, title?, body?, color? }` |
| `PATCH`  | `/admin/notes/:id` | update title/body/color |
| `DELETE` | `/admin/notes/:id` | delete |

Service enforces owner XOR + owner-exists + not-soft-deleted, and picks the next `orderIndex` on create.

### DTO cleanup
- `create-story.dto.ts` / `create-chapter.dto.ts`: removed the `notes` field. With `forbidNonWhitelisted: true` the API now **400s** if `notes` is in a story/chapter body — the frontend PR will route note edits to `/admin/notes`.

This migration drops the legacy `notes` columns after backfill. The **old frontend** still sends `notes` in the story/chapter save body and reads `notes` from the story/chapter GET response. So:

content.text:
Merged into `develop` (PR [#180](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/lucifers-diary/pull/180)).

## What was actually wrong

PR #179 set `max-height` when a note was open — that's the *upper bound*, not a guarantee. The sticky panel was still **content-sized**, so its real height only stretched to wherever the last pill ended. That's exactly the empty green-box space you marked.

## The fix
Two CSS lines did it:
- **`min-height: calc(100dvh - 90px)`** when `.hasExpanded` — forces the panel to fill all the way down, not just allow it.
- **`top: 76px`** (was 12px) — sits the panel below the sticky admin top bar (~66px tall, `z-index: 90`) instead of slipping behind it.

Now when you click a note, the right column becomes a full-height writing surface from the bottom of the nav to the bottom of the viewport, and the expanded card's textarea flex-fills the available space.

## Redeploy + look
Frontend CSS-only — quick:
```bash
cd /www/wwwroot/luciferdiary/frontend && git pull && npm ci && npm run rebuild
pm2 restart lucifer-web
```

If it's still not filling all the way (or it's *too* tall — overlapping the page header), tell me and I'll tweak the `top: 76px` offset. The 76px is my estimate of nav height + a tiny gap; the real measurement may differ slightly.

Reminder: still on `develop` along with #177, #178, #179. Nothing on `main` yet.

Merged into `develop` (PR [#181](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/lucifers-diary/pull/181)).

## What you'll feel on the dev server

**On a pill (collapsed note)**
- Hover → 1px lift + soft glow tinted to the note's own color (red note → red glow, gold note → gold glow). Border highlights to the note color.
- Press → settles back with a tiny `scale(0.995)`. Feels physical.

**When you open a note**
- The new expanded view does a brief opacity + 3px lift-in (200ms, ease-out-quart). Covers both clicking a pill *and* hitting "+ Add note" (since new notes spawn expanded).

**When you open the 3-dot menu**
- Pops in from the **top-right corner** (where the trigger sits) — 160ms fade + scale.

**+ Add note button**
- Same gold-CTA hover lift the landing page's *Start Reading* uses, so the brand affordance is consistent.

**The panel growing tall when you open a note** (the request you actually asked about)
- Was snapping before — now glides with a **260ms ease-out-quart** curve on `top`, `min-height`, and `max-height` together. So opening a note feels like the panel *breathes open*.

**Accessibility kept**
- Both modules add a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block — anyone with OS-level Reduce Motion on gets the same layout with all animations stripped. Matches the existing GSAP pattern in `SiteHeader`.

## Redeploy + look
CSS-only — frontend rebuild + restart, no backend touched:
```bash
cd /www/wwwroot/luciferdiary/frontend && git pull && npm ci && npm run rebuild
pm2 restart lucifer-web
```

Test pass: hover a pill, click it open, watch the panel grow, open the menu. If anything feels too much (animation too long, glow too strong) or too little, tell me what and I'll tune the easing/timing/intensity.

Still on `develop` — PRs [#177](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/lucifers-diary/pull/177)–[#181](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/lucifers-diary/pull/181) stacked, `main` untouched.

## T1 — Add macOS-dock proximity hover to public card rows + admin notes list
plugin: gsap core (gsap.quickTo, no plugin registration needed)
demo: https://demos.gsap.com/demo/macos-dock-effect/ (CodePen source https://codepen.io/GreenSock/pen/PwNeKZy)
PRs: 2
use case: When the cursor moves over a row/grid of story cards (and the admin notes pill list), nearby items scale and lift in proportion to cursor distance so the row feels alive and tactile.
files to change: frontend/components/ExpandableSection.tsx, frontend/components/CardGrid.tsx, frontend/components/ContinueReadingRow.tsx, frontend/components/ResumeReadingRow.tsx, frontend/components/StoryCard.module.css, frontend/components/ContinueCard.module.css, frontend/components/ContinueReadingRow.module.css, frontend/app/page.tsx, frontend/app/page.module.css, frontend/app/admin/_components/NotesPanel.tsx, frontend/app/admin/_components/NoteCard.tsx, frontend/app/admin/_components/NoteCard.module.css, frontend/app/admin/_components/NotesPanel.module.css
files to create: frontend/lib/useDockProximity.ts
approach: Create a shared `useDockProximity(containerRef, { axis, radius, maxScale, maxLift })` hook in `frontend/lib/useDockProximity.ts` that wraps the canonical pattern in a `useGSAP({ scope: containerRef })` call: on mount it grabs the direct-child elements that carry a `data-dock-item` attribute, builds a `gsap.quickTo(child, 'scale')` and `gsap.quickTo(child, 'y')` setter pair per child, caches each child's center via `getBoundingClientRect()`, and attaches a single `pointermove` on the container plus `pointerleave` (tween back to scale 1 / y 0). The hook bails synchronously when `prefersReducedMotion()` is true and gates the listener install on `window.matchMedia('(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)').matches` so touch devices opt out. It re-measures on `ResizeObserver` of the container and on a passed `deps` array (children-count dependency) so newly mounted cards get setters. Wire it into the five existing container refs — `ExpandableSection`, `CardGrid`, `ContinueReadingRow` (add a `listRef`), `ResumeReadingRow` (add a `listRef`), a new tiny client wrapper for the homepage hero `.heroCardsList`, and `NotesPanel` `<div className={styles.list}>` (axis: 'y' for the vertical notes column, axis: 'x' everywhere else). Add `data-dock-item` to each card root (StoryCard / SeriesCard / ChapterCard / ContinueCard / inline ContinueReadingRow card / NoteCard collapsed pill) and drop the CSS `:hover { transform: translateY(-2px) }` rules from those card stylesheets — GSAP owns transform now, CSS keeps `border-color` / `box-shadow` hover. In `NotesPanel` the hook is also gated on `expandedId == null` and re-runs when `notes.length` changes.
risks: CSS hover transforms on cards (translateY -2px in StoryCard/ContinueCard/NoteCard) will fight per-frame GSAP transform writes — must be removed from CSS for the affected pills. | Cards have `transition: transform var(--transition-fast)` which re-eases every GSAP write — needs to be scoped away (e.g. transition only border-color/box-shadow on the relevant elements). | NotesPanel `.list` is `flex-direction: column`, so the dock is vertical — confirm with user that vertical magnification is acceptable (a real macOS dock is horizontal). | On `/series/[id]` `ChapterList` is a vertical full-width list, not a rail — probably should NOT get the dock effect (clarify). | Existing GSAP scroll-reveal stagger in CardGrid/ExpandableSection writes to opacity/y on first scroll-in; needs `overwrite: 'auto'` on the dock setters to avoid clashing. | ResizeObserver + double-rAF needed on first measure so cards have laid out before centers are cached.
reduced motion: Hook checks `prefersReducedMotion()` from `@/lib/gsap` on mount AND subscribes to the matchMedia change event; when reduced motion is active it returns early without installing listeners or building setters, so the row keeps its un-animated CSS resting state.

## T2 — Animate auto-height when expanding an admin note
plugin: gsap core (measure-then-tween height pattern)
demo: https://demos.gsap.com/demo/animate-auto-height/
PRs: 1
use case: When the user clicks a collapsed note pill in the admin NotesPanel, the panel smoothly grows from its current height to the natural height of the expanded card instead of snapping to a CSS keyframe.
files to change: frontend/app/admin/_components/NotesPanel.tsx, frontend/app/admin/_components/NoteCard.tsx, frontend/app/admin/_components/NoteCard.module.css
files to create: frontend/app/admin/_components/AutoHeightPanel.tsx
approach: Add a small `AutoHeightPanel` client component (under admin/_components) that takes `open: boolean` + children, wraps them in a `<div ref={panelRef} style={{ height: 0, overflow: 'hidden' }}>`, and uses `useGSAP(() => {...}, { scope: panelRef, dependencies: [open] })` to run the canonical measure-then-tween: read `startH = getBoundingClientRect().height`, set `height: auto` to read `fullH`, then `gsap.fromTo(el, { height: startH }, { height: open ? fullH : 0, duration: 0.35, ease: 'power2.inOut', onComplete: () => { if (open) gsap.set(el, { height: 'auto', overflow: '' }) } })`. In `NoteCard.tsx` the expanded body (currently rendered conditionally inside the expanded branch with a `noteExpandIn` keyframe) is wrapped in `<AutoHeightPanel open={expanded}>...</AutoHeightPanel>` so the React tree always renders both branches, with the panel collapsing to 0px when not expanded. Remove the `animation: noteExpandIn 200ms` rule from `NoteCard.module.css` so GSAP owns the entrance; keep the swap-in opacity fade as a tiny child tween started in `onStart`. Reduced-motion path: when `prefersReducedMotion()` is true, the hook skips the tween and just `gsap.set(el, { height: open ? 'auto' : 0 })` synchronously. Cleanup is automatic via `useGSAP` revert on unmount; `overflow: hidden` is removed on complete so focus rings and dropdown menus inside the expanded note are not clipped.
risks: The current `noteExpandIn` keyframe and the panel's existing 260ms max-height transition on `.panel` (hasExpanded toggle) could double-animate — the panel-level transition must stay (it grows the aside), and only the per-note body grows via GSAP. | Re-measuring on every `open` change is correct, but if the note's content changes while open (e.g. typing), height freezes at `auto` so it grows naturally — verify this works inside the existing contenteditable / textarea. | Color picker / 3-dot menu popovers inside the note must not be clipped — ensure `overflow: ''` is restored on complete and never re-applied while open. | Focus management: when collapsing a note that contains a focused textarea, focus should be moved out before the height tween so it doesn't land in a 0-height region.
reduced motion: `AutoHeightPanel` checks `prefersReducedMotion()` at the start of the `useGSAP` callback and substitutes a synchronous `gsap.set(el, { height: open ? 'auto' : 0 })` instead of the fromTo tween.

## T3 — Add GSAP click feedback to Like / Save / Share with per-button color flash
plugin: gsap core (timeline with elastic.out + back.out + CSS variable tween)
demo: https://codepen.io/GreenSock/pen/RwMQwpR (canonical `gsap.matchMedia` reduced-motion gate) + https://github.com/greensock/react#contextsafe (useGSAP + contextSafe click handler pattern)
PRs: 1
use case: When a reader clicks LIKE, SAVE, or SHARE in the reading footer, the pill plays a short, tactile scale+color-flash so the action feels acknowledged even before the network round-trip completes.
files to change: frontend/components/LikeButton.tsx, frontend/components/LikeButton.module.css, frontend/components/SaveButton.tsx, frontend/components/SaveButton.module.css, frontend/components/ShareButton.tsx, frontend/components/ShareButton.module.css, frontend/components/QuoteShare.tsx
files to create: 
approach: Define a tiny shared helper `pulseButton(el, color)` (inline in each component, or factored into `frontend/lib/buttonPulse.ts` if all three end up identical) that builds a `gsap.timeline({ defaults: { overwrite: 'auto' } })` of: `.to(el, { scale: 0.88, duration: 0.08, ease: 'power2.out' })` then `.to(el, { scale: 1, duration: 0.42, ease: 'back.out(2.4)' })`, plus a parallel `.fromTo(el, { '--pulse-flash': 0 }, { '--pulse-flash': 1, duration: 0.18, ease: 'power1.out' }, 0).to(el, { '--pulse-flash': 0, duration: 0.25, ease: 'power1.in' }, 0.18)`. Each button's CSS module gets a `box-shadow: 0 0 0 calc(var(--pulse-flash, 0) * 6px) color-mix(in oklab, transparent, var(--button-color) calc(var(--pulse-flash, 0) * 60%))` so the color flash is a per-button glow keyed off a CSS variable — `--button-color` is `--like` on LikeButton, `--gold` on SaveButton, and `--gold-soft` (or `--text-muted`) on ShareButton (final palette per the open question). LikeButton already has the ref + useGSAP scope; SaveButton needs `useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null)`, `useGSAP({ scope: buttonRef })`, and the `contextSafe`-wrapped `pulse()` call at the top of `toggle()` (skipping the anonymous Link variant entirely). ShareButton gets the same treatment, called at the top of `onShare`. QuoteShare wires a one-shot `gsap.fromTo(e.currentTarget, { scale: 1 }, { scale: 1.12, yoyo: true, repeat: 1, duration: 0.1, ease: 'power2.out' })` from inside `onShareClick(target, i, e)` — color flash optional there since the existing `.buttonCopied` gold flash already covers confirmation. Every pulse is guarded by `prefersReducedMotion()` (state still flips, motion is skipped), and `gsap.killTweensOf` at the top of the handler so spam-clicks restart cleanly rather than queue.
risks: LikeButton's existing `pulse()` uses scale 1.15 on a yoyo — the new 0.88→1 elastic feel will differ visually; should still match the rest of the row. | CSS variable tweening through `gsap.to(el, { '--pulse-flash': 1 })` requires that the variable exist as a registered custom property OR be referenced in a style declaration on the element — using it inside `box-shadow` keeps it live without needing `@property`. | SaveButton anonymous variant is an `<a>` Link — must NOT attach the pulse there. | ShareButton sits in the same row as Like/Save and uses neutral colors; if the flash color isn't tied to a real `--share` token, choose a neutral (`--text-muted` or `--gold-soft`) to avoid implying a 'success' meaning. | QuoteShare's brand buttons (X/Facebook/Bluesky) call `dismiss()` immediately after `window.open`, killing the popover and the in-flight tween — that's fine but be aware the visual is truncated.
reduced motion: `pulse()` short-circuits when `prefersReducedMotion()` returns true; the optimistic state still flips and aria-pressed updates so the action remains fully usable, just without motion.

## T4 — Tween scroll restore back to last reading position with ScrollToPlugin
plugin: ScrollToPlugin (free, gsap core distribution)
demo: https://gsap.com/docs/v3/Plugins/ScrollToPlugin/
PRs: 1
use case: When a returning reader opens a story or chapter they were partway through, the page smoothly animates the window down to their saved scroll offset instead of snapping with `behavior: 'instant'`.
files to change: frontend/lib/gsap.ts, frontend/lib/useReadingPosition.ts
files to create: 
approach: Register ScrollToPlugin in `frontend/lib/gsap.ts` alongside ScrollTrigger inside the existing `typeof window !== 'undefined'` guard and re-export it. In `frontend/lib/useReadingPosition.ts`, swap the single `window.scrollTo({ top: target, behavior: 'instant' })` call inside `restore()` for a `gsap.to(window, { duration: 1.1, scrollTo: { y: Math.min(target, doc.scrollHeight - innerHeight), autoKill: true, onAutoKill: () => { /* no-op */ } }, ease: 'power2.out', overwrite: 'auto' })`, keeping the existing `requestIdleCallback`/rAF deferral and the `>= RESTORE_MIN_PERCENT` gate. Add three early bails before the tween: (a) if `prefersReducedMotion()` from `@/lib/gsap` is true, fall back to the existing `window.scrollTo({ top: target, behavior: 'instant' })`; (b) if `window.location.hash.includes(':~:text=')` OR `window.location.hash.length > 1`, skip entirely so `TextFragmentScroller` (or native Chromium fragment directive) owns the arrival; (c) if `Math.abs(window.scrollY) > 50` (user has already scrolled before rIC fired), skip. Capture the tween in a local `tween` variable and call `tween.kill()` in the existing `cancelled`/cleanup path so a route-change mid-tween does not keep scrolling the next page. Do not extend `TextFragmentScroller`; do not refactor into a separate component.
risks: Document height can shift after hydration (font load, image swap, async RichText) — `target` may exceed scrollMax; clamp via `Math.min(target, doc.scrollHeight - innerHeight)` to avoid landing short. | If `html { scroll-behavior: smooth }` is ever set globally it will fight ScrollToPlugin and break `autoKill` — verify globals.css has none, and add a comment in `lib/gsap.ts` warning future contributors. | Chrome trackpad `wheel` autoKill historically under-fires — may need a belt-and-braces `wheel`/`touchstart` listener calling `gsap.killTweensOf(window)` as backup. | Page-change (paged-mode `goToPage`) currently uses `behavior: 'auto'` — leave that alone; only the saved-position restore is in scope. | Hash precedence: a deep-link to `#:~:text=...` from a shared quote MUST win over the stored heuristic restore — handled by the early bail.
reduced motion: `restore()` calls `prefersReducedMotion()` before constructing the tween and falls back to the original `window.scrollTo({ top: target, behavior: 'instant' })` synchronous jump when true.

## T5 — Animate tag-filter reorders with GSAP Flip on browse / search / tag
plugin: Flip (free, gsap core distribution)
demo: https://demos.gsap.com/demo/animate-between-different-targets/ (Flip plugin hub: https://demos.gsap.com/plugin/flip/)
PRs: 2
use case: When the user toggles a tag in the TagBar (or the admin TagPicker / BlockedTagsButton tag list), the cards smoothly Flip from their old grid positions to the new filtered positions instead of snapping after a server navigation.
files to change: frontend/lib/gsap.ts, frontend/components/TagBar.tsx, frontend/components/CardGrid.tsx, frontend/components/StoryCard.tsx, frontend/components/SeriesCard.tsx, frontend/components/BlockedTagsButton.tsx, frontend/app/admin/_components/TagPicker.tsx
files to create: frontend/lib/flipBridge.ts
approach: Register `Flip` in `frontend/lib/gsap.ts` and re-export. For the public browse/search/tag surfaces — server-driven filtering is the load-bearing constraint, so use the lightest of the three workarounds in the inventory: `TagBar` keeps `<Link>` but intercepts the click with `e.preventDefault()`, synchronously calls `Flip.getState('[data-flip-id]', { props: 'opacity' })`, stores the state in a module-level Map (`frontend/lib/flipBridge.ts`) keyed by a session-scoped token derived from the new path+query, then `router.push(href)`. After the server navigation commits, `CardGrid`'s `useGSAP` (keyed on serialised `tagIds` from `useSearchParams`) drains the stored state and runs `Flip.from(state, { duration: 0.55, ease: 'power2.inOut', absolute: true, stagger: 0.02, onEnter: el => gsap.fromTo(el, { opacity: 0, scale: 0.92 }, { opacity: 1, scale: 1, duration: 0.35 }), onLeave: el => gsap.to(el, { opacity: 0, scale: 0.92, duration: 0.25 }) })`. Cards expose `data-flip-id={story.id || series.id}` on their root so the matcher survives a React re-mount. The bridge clears itself after `Flip.from` completes and on a timeout fallback (so a back-navigation doesn't apply stale state to a different route). For the two purely client-side surfaces — `BlockedTagsButton` and admin `TagPicker` — drop Flip in directly around the existing `useMemo` sort: capture before the toggle setState in the click handler, run `Flip.from` in a `useLayoutEffect` keyed on the order signature. Reduced-motion: skip `Flip.getState` entirely so the bridge stores nothing and the next render just commits without animation. CardGrid's existing scroll-reveal stagger (`once: true`) is guarded to not re-run after the first mount, so it won't fight the Flip tween — but add an `overwrite: 'auto'` on the Flip tween for safety.
risks: Server-side filtering means new DOM nodes — the bridge approach relies on Flip's `data-flip-id` matching surviving cards across a route change; if React's reconciler can't preserve the grid container between server renders, only `onEnter` will fire (degraded but not broken). | Module-level state survives route changes but also survives them too well — must clear after Flip.from completes AND on a setTimeout fallback (1.5s) so a back-button or fast tag-toggle doesn't apply stale 'before' positions to a different result set. | App Router prefetch + cache may make the navigation feel near-instant; need to verify that `useGSAP` keyed on `useSearchParams` actually re-runs after the server navigation (not just on the first render). | `absolute: true` briefly pulls cards out of flow during the tween — the CardGrid container must have a stable height during the tween or items below will jump; may need `Flip.from(state, { absolute: true, simple: true })` with a held min-height during animation. | If the grid is wrapped in `<Suspense>` with streaming, the cards may mount in batches — Flip would only see the first batch's positions; verify with the actual streaming behavior or fall back to capturing onComplete from the navigation event. | Tags can ALSO be filtered by navigating to `/tag/[slug]` — that's a different route entirely and the Flip bridge won't span it; scope this PR to TagBar-driven reorders within /search and document /tag/[slug] as out of scope. | BlockedTagsButton and TagPicker are unaffected by the routing complexity — they should land first as a proof-of-concept before the browse path.

Add `data-dock-item` to each card root (StoryCard / SeriesCard / ChapterCard / ContinueCard / inline ContinueReadingRow card / NoteCard collapsed pill) and drop the CSS `:hover { transform: translateY(-2px) }` rules from those card stylesheets — GSAP owns transform now, CSS keeps `border-color` / `box-shadow` hover. In `NotesPanel` the hook is also gated on `expandedId == null` and re-runs when `notes.length` changes.
risks: CSS hover transforms on cards (translateY -2px in StoryCard/ContinueCard/NoteCard) will fight per-frame GSAP transform writes — must be removed from CSS for the affected pills. | Cards have `transition: transform var(--transition-fast)` which re-eases every GSAP write — needs to be scoped away (e.g. transition only border-color/box-shadow on the relevant elements). | NotesPanel `.list` is `flex-direction: column`, so the dock is vertical — confirm with user that vertical magnification is acceptable (a real macOS dock is horizontal). | On `/series/[id]` `ChapterList` is a vertical full-width list, not a rail — probably should NOT get the dock effect (clarify). | Existing GSAP scroll-reveal stagger in CardGrid/ExpandableSection writes to opacity/y on first scroll-in; needs `overwrite: 'auto'` on the dock setters to avoid clashing. | ResizeObserver + double-rAF needed on first measure so cards have laid out before centers are cached.
reduced motion: Hook checks `prefersReducedMotion()` from `@/lib/gsap` on mount AND subscribes to the matchMedia change event; when reduced motion is active it returns early without installing listeners or building setters, so the row keeps its un-animated CSS resting state.

## T2 — Animate auto-height when expanding an admin note
plugin: gsap core (measure-then-tween height pattern)
demo: https://demos.gsap.com/demo/animate-auto-height/
PRs: 1
use case: When the user clicks a collapsed note pill in the admin NotesPanel, the panel smoothly grows from its current height to the natural height of the expanded card instead of snapping to a CSS keyframe.
files to change: frontend/app/admin/_components/NotesPanel.tsx, frontend/app/admin/_components/NoteCard.tsx, frontend/app/admin/_components/NoteCard.module.css
files to create: frontend/app/admin/_components/AutoHeightPanel.tsx
approach: Add a small `AutoHeightPanel` client component (under admin/_components) that takes `open: boolean` + children, wraps them in a `<div ref={panelRef} style={{ height: 0, overflow: 'hidden' }}>`, and uses `useGSAP(() => {...}, { scope: panelRef, dependencies: [open] })` to run the canonical measure-then-tween: read `startH = getBoundingClientRect().height`, set `height: auto` to read `fullH`, then `gsap.fromTo(el, { height: startH }, { height: open ? fullH : 0, duration: 0.35, ease: 'power2.inOut', onComplete: () => { if (open) gsap.set(el, { height: 'auto', overflow: '' }) } })`. In `NoteCard.tsx` the expanded body (currently rendered conditionally inside the expanded branch with a `noteExpandIn` keyframe) is wrapped in `<AutoHeightPanel open={expanded}>...</AutoHeightPanel>` so the React tree always renders both branches, with the panel collapsing to 0px when not expanded. Remove the `animation: noteExpandIn 200ms` rule from `NoteCard.module.css` so GSAP owns the entrance; keep the swap-in opacity fade as a tiny child tween started in `onStart`. Reduced-motion path: when `prefersReducedMotion()` is true, the hook skips the tween and just `gsap.set(el, { height: open ? 'auto' : 0 })` synchronously. Cleanup is automatic via `useGSAP` revert on unmount; `overflow: hidden` is removed on complete so focus rings and dropdown menus inside the expanded note are not clipped.
risks: The current `noteExpandIn` keyframe and the panel's existing 260ms max-height transition on `.panel` (hasExpanded toggle) could double-animate — the panel-level transition must stay (it grows the aside), and only the per-note body grows via GSAP. | Re-measuring on every `open` change is correct, but if the note's content changes while open (e.g. typing), height freezes at `auto` so it grows naturally — verify this works inside the existing contenteditable / textarea. | Color picker / 3-dot menu popovers inside the note must not be clipped — ensure `overflow: ''` is restored on complete and never re-applied while open. | Focus management: when collapsing a note that contains a focused textarea, focus should be moved out before the height tween so it doesn't land in a 0-height region.
reduced motion: `AutoHeightPanel` checks `prefersReducedMotion()` at the start of the `useGSAP` callback and substitutes a synchronous `gsap.set(el, { height: open ? 'auto' : 0 })` instead of the fromTo tween.

## T3 — Add GSAP click feedback to Like / Save / Share with per-button color flash
plugin: gsap core (timeline with elastic.out + back.out + CSS variable tween)
demo: https://codepen.io/GreenSock/pen/RwMQwpR (canonical `gsap.matchMedia` reduced-motion gate) + https://github.com/greensock/react#contextsafe (useGSAP + contextSafe click handler pattern)
PRs: 1
use case: When a reader clicks LIKE, SAVE, or SHARE in the reading footer, the pill plays a short, tactile scale+color-flash so the action feels acknowledged even before the network round-trip completes.
files to change: frontend/components/LikeButton.tsx, frontend/components/LikeButton.module.css, frontend/components/SaveButton.tsx, frontend/components/SaveButton.module.css, frontend/components/ShareButton.tsx, frontend/components/ShareButton.module.css, frontend/components/QuoteShare.tsx
files to create: 
approach: Define a tiny shared helper `pulseButton(el, color)` (inline in each component, or factored into `frontend/lib/buttonPulse.ts` if all three end up identical) that builds a `gsap.timeline({ defaults: { overwrite: 'auto' } })` of: `.to(el, { scale: 0.88, duration: 0.08, ease: 'power2.out' })` then `.to(el, { scale: 1, duration: 0.42, ease: 'back.out(2.4)' })`, plus a parallel `.fromTo(el, { '--pulse-flash': 0 }, { '--pulse-flash': 1, duration: 0.18, ease: 'power1.out' }, 0).to(el, { '--pulse-flash': 0, duration: 0.25, ease: 'power1.in' }, 0.18)`. Each button's CSS module gets a `box-shadow: 0 0 0 calc(var(--pulse-flash, 0) * 6px) color-mix(in oklab, transparent, var(--button-color) calc(var(--pulse-flash, 0) * 60%))` so the color flash is a per-button glow keyed off a CSS variable — `--button-color` is `--like` on LikeButton, `--gold` on SaveButton, and `--gold-soft` (or `--text-muted`) on ShareButton (final palette per the open question). LikeButton already has the ref + useGSAP scope; SaveButton needs `useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null)`, `useGSAP({ scope: buttonRef })`, and the `contextSafe`-wrapped `pulse()` call at the top of `toggle()` (skipping the anonymous Link variant entirely). ShareButton gets the same treatment, called at the top of `onShare`. QuoteShare wires a one-shot `gsap.fromTo(e.currentTarget, { scale: 1 }, { scale: 1.12, yoyo: true, repeat: 1, duration: 0.1, ease: 'power2.out' })` from inside `onShareClick(target, i, e)` — color flash optional there since the existing `.buttonCopied` gold flash already covers confirmation. Every pulse is guarded by `prefersReducedMotion()` (state still flips, motion is skipped), and `gsap.killTweensOf` at the top of the handler so spam-clicks restart cleanly rather than queue.
risks: LikeButton's existing `pulse()` uses scale 1.15 on a yoyo — the new 0.88→1 elastic feel will differ visually; should still match the rest of the row. | CSS variable tweening through `gsap.to(el, { '--pulse-flash': 1 })` requires that the variable exist as a registered custom property OR be referenced in a style declaration on the element — using it inside `box-shadow` keeps it live without needing `@property`. | SaveButton anonymous variant is an `<a>` Link — must NOT attach the pulse there. | ShareButton sits in the same row as Like/Save and uses neutral colors; if the flash color isn't tied to a real `--share` token, choose a neutral (`--text-muted` or `--gold-soft`) to avoid implying a 'success' meaning. | QuoteShare's brand buttons (X/Facebook/Bluesky) call `dismiss()` immediately after `window.open`, killing the popover and the in-flight tween — that's fine but be aware the visual is truncated.
reduced motion: `pulse()` short-circuits when `prefersReducedMotion()` returns true; the optimistic state still flips and aria-pressed updates so the action remains fully usable, just without motion.

## T4 — Tween scroll restore back to last reading position with ScrollToPlugin
plugin: ScrollToPlugin (free, gsap core distribution)
demo: https://gsap.com/docs/v3/Plugins/ScrollToPlugin/
PRs: 1
use case: When a returning reader opens a story or chapter they were partway through, the page smoothly animates the window down to their saved scroll offset instead of snapping with `behavior: 'instant'`.
files to change: frontend/lib/gsap.ts, frontend/lib/useReadingPosition.ts
files to create: 
approach: Register ScrollToPlugin in `frontend/lib/gsap.ts` alongside ScrollTrigger inside the existing `typeof window !== 'undefined'` guard and re-export it. In `frontend/lib/useReadingPosition.ts`, swap the single `window.scrollTo({ top: target, behavior: 'instant' })` call inside `restore()` for a `gsap.to(window, { duration: 1.1, scrollTo: { y: Math.min(target, doc.scrollHeight - innerHeight), autoKill: true, onAutoKill: () => { /* no-op */ } }, ease: 'power2.out', overwrite: 'auto' })`, keeping the existing `requestIdleCallback`/rAF deferral and the `>= RESTORE_MIN_PERCENT` gate. Add three early bails before the tween: (a) if `prefersReducedMotion()` from `@/lib/gsap` is true, fall back to the existing `window.scrollTo({ top: target, behavior: 'instant' })`; (b) if `window.location.hash.includes(':~:text=')` OR `window.location.hash.length > 1`, skip entirely so `TextFragmentScroller` (or native Chromium fragment directive) owns the arrival; (c) if `Math.abs(window.scrollY) > 50` (user has already scrolled before rIC fired), skip. Capture the tween in a local `tween` variable and call `tween.kill()` in the existing `cancelled`/cleanup path so a route-change mid-tween does not keep scrolling the next page. Do not extend `TextFragmentScroller`; do not refactor into a separate component.
risks: Document height can shift after hydration (font load, image swap, async RichText) — `target` may exceed scrollMax; clamp via `Math.min(target, doc.scrollHeight - innerHeight)` to avoid landing short. | If `html { scroll-behavior: smooth }` is ever set globally it will fight ScrollToPlugin and break `autoKill` — verify globals.css has none, and add a comment in `lib/gsap.ts` warning future contributors. | Chrome trackpad `wheel` autoKill historically under-fires — may need a belt-and-braces `wheel`/`touchstart` listener calling `gsap.killTweensOf(window)` as backup. | Page-change (paged-mode `goToPage`) currently uses `behavior: 'auto'` — leave that alone; only the saved-position restore is in scope. | Hash precedence: a deep-link to `#:~:text=...` from a shared quote MUST win over the stored heuristic restore — handled by the early bail.
reduced motion: `restore()` calls `prefersReducedMotion()` before constructing the tween and falls back to the original `window.scrollTo({ top: target, behavior: 'instant' })` synchronous jump when true.

## T5 — Animate tag-filter reorders with GSAP Flip on browse / search / tag
plugin: Flip (free, gsap core distribution)
demo: https://demos.gsap.com/demo/animate-between-different-targets/ (Flip plugin hub: https://demos.gsap.com/plugin/flip/)
PRs: 2
use case: When the user toggles a tag in the TagBar (or the admin TagPicker / BlockedTagsButton tag list), the cards smoothly Flip from their old grid positions to the new filtered positions instead of snapping after a server navigation.
files to change: frontend/lib/gsap.ts, frontend/components/TagBar.tsx, frontend/components/CardGrid.tsx, frontend/components/StoryCard.tsx, frontend/components/SeriesCard.tsx, frontend/components/BlockedTagsButton.tsx, frontend/app/admin/_components/TagPicker.tsx
files to create: frontend/lib/flipBridge.ts
approach: Register `Flip` in `frontend/lib/gsap.ts` and re-export. For the public browse/search/tag surfaces — server-driven filtering is the load-bearing constraint, so use the lightest of the three workarounds in the inventory: `TagBar` keeps `<Link>` but intercepts the click with `e.preventDefault()`, synchronously calls `Flip.getState('[data-flip-id]', { props: 'opacity' })`, stores the state in a module-level Map (`frontend/lib/flipBridge.ts`) keyed by a session-scoped token derived from the new path+query, then `router.push(href)`. After the server navigation commits, `CardGrid`'s `useGSAP` (keyed on serialised `tagIds` from `useSearchParams`) drains the stored state and runs `Flip.from(state, { duration: 0.55, ease: 'power2.inOut', absolute: true, stagger: 0.02, onEnter: el => gsap.fromTo(el, { opacity: 0, scale: 0.92 }, { opacity: 1, scale: 1, duration: 0.35 }), onLeave: el => gsap.to(el, { opacity: 0, scale: 0.92, duration: 0.25 }) })`. Cards expose `data-flip-id={story.id || series.id}` on their root so the matcher survives a React re-mount. The bridge clears itself after `Flip.from` completes and on a timeout fallback (so a back-navigation doesn't apply stale state to a different route). For the two purely client-side surfaces — `BlockedTagsButton` and admin `TagPicker` — drop Flip in directly around the existing `useMemo` sort: capture before the toggle setState in the click handler, run `Flip.from` in a `useLayoutEffect` keyed on the order signature. Reduced-motion: skip `Flip.getState` entirely so the bridge stores nothing and the next render just commits without animation. CardGrid's existing scroll-reveal stagger (`once: true`) is guarded to not re-run after the first mount, so it won't fight the Flip tween — but add an `overwrite: 'auto'` on the Flip tween for safety.
risks: Server-side filtering means new DOM nodes — the bridge approach relies on Flip's `data-flip-id` matching surviving cards across a route change; if React's reconciler can't preserve the grid container between server renders, only `onEnter` will fire (degraded but not broken). | Module-level state survives route changes but also survives them too well — must clear after Flip.from completes AND on a setTimeout fallback (1.5s) so a back-button or fast tag-toggle doesn't apply stale 'before' positions to a different result set. | App Router prefetch + cache may make the navigation feel near-instant; need to verify that `useGSAP` keyed on `useSearchParams` actually re-runs after the server navigation (not just on the first render). | `absolute: true` briefly pulls cards out of flow during the tween — the CardGrid container must have a stable height during the tween or items below will jump; may need `Flip.from(state, { absolute: true, simple: true })` with a held min-height during animation. | If the grid is wrapped in `<Suspense>` with streaming, the cards may mount in batches — Flip would only see the first batch's positions; verify with the actual streaming behavior or fall back to capturing onComplete from the navigation event. | Tags can ALSO be filtered by navigating to `/tag/[slug]` — that's a different route entirely and the Flip bridge won't span it; scope this PR to TagBar-driven reorders within /search and document /tag/[slug] as out of scope. | BlockedTagsButton and TagPicker are unaffected by the routing complexity — they should land first as a proof-of-concept before the browse path.
reduced motion: TagBar's click handler wraps the `Flip.getState` capture in `if (!prefersReducedMotion()) { ... }`, so under reduced motion the bridge stays empty and CardGrid's `useGSAP` short-circuits to render-with-no-animation (the existing snap behavior).

content.content:
=== SUGGESTED SEQUENCE ===
T3: Lowest-risk and most isolated (3 small components, no new infra, no routing surgery). Shipping it first proves the per-button color-flash CSS variable pattern and warms the team up on the `useGSAP` + `contextSafe` idiom that T1/T2/T5 also use.
T4: Self-contained one-line swap inside an existing hook plus a `lib/gsap.ts` plugin registration; depends on nothing else but unblocks T5 because T5 will also touch `lib/gsap.ts` (Flip registration) — landing T4 first sets the precedent for how new plugins get registered.
T2: Admin-only surface, smallest visual footprint, and the `AutoHeightPanel` component is reusable — landing it before T1 means T1's NotesPanel work can compose with it cleanly (an expanded note inside the dock-list still needs to grow smoothly).
T1: Public-site visual change touching many files; sequencing it after T2 lets the admin notes integration benefit from the AutoHeightPanel already being in place. The shared `useDockProximity` hook is also the first piece of GSAP infrastructure that needs `data-*` attributes on card roots — useful precedent for T5's `data-flip-id`.
T5: Highest-risk and biggest unknown (server-driven routing vs Flip's in-place DOM contract). Saving it for last lets us ship the two purely client-side Flip surfaces (BlockedTagsButton, TagPicker) as a small first PR to prove the integration, then tackle the server-routing flipBridge in a second PR with all other GSAP infrastructure already battle-tested.

=== OPEN QUESTIONS ===
     1	T5 (CRITICAL): The browse/search/tag pages filter server-side via App Router navigation, so cards are brand-new React/DOM nodes on each filter click. The plan uses a module-level `flipBridge` Map keyed by a path+query token to hand Flip state across the navigation — this is the lightest workaround but depends on React's reconciler preserving the CardGrid container across server renders. Are you OK with this risk profile, or would you rather (a) convert /search and /tag to client-side filtering (loses SSR result counts, breaks /tag/[slug] SEO landing), or (b) hybrid (over-fetch + client filter + reconcile, most work, smoothest UX)? Without a decision here T5 is the hardest task to scope.
     2	T5: Should `/tag/[slug]` pages get the Flip reorder too? Right now navigating to /tag/[slug] is a different route entirely and the bridge won't span it cleanly. Plan currently scopes T5 to TagBar-on-/search reorders only. Confirm /tag/[slug] is acceptable as out-of-scope.
     3	T4: When a returning reader arrives via a `#:~:text=...` shared quote URL, who should win — the saved-position restore, or the text-fragment scroll? Plan defaults to text-fragment wins (skip the restore tween entirely if any hash is present). Confirm or override.
     4	T4: Tween duration of 1.1s with `power2.out` and `autoKill: true` is the default; do you want a distance-aware duration (longer trips take ~1.6s, short ~0.6s) or a fixed 1.1s for everyone?
     5	T3: What `--button-color` should ShareButton flash use? Plan candidates: `--gold-soft` (matches the existing Save token family, reads as a neutral confirmation) or `--text-muted` (most neutral, no implicit success meaning) or introduce a new `--share` token. LikeButton = `--like`, SaveButton = `--gold` are unambiguous; ShareButton is the only one without a clear active-color token.
     6	T3: Should the popover entrance in QuoteShare (currently a 140ms CSS `quoteShareIn` keyframe added in PR #181) be converted to GSAP in this same PR, or left alone and tackled as a follow-up (recommended in the inventory)?
     7	T1: Admin NotesPanel `.list` is `flex-direction: column`, so the dock-proximity will magnify vertically (cursor Y distance), not horizontally like a real macOS dock. Is vertical magnification the desired effect, or should the layout be flipped to horizontal first (which conflicts with the panel's `overflow-y: auto` scroll)?
     8	T1: `/series/[id]` `ChapterList` is a vertical full-width row list, not a horizontal rail. Plan currently excludes it from the dock effect (the lift/scale would feel wrong on full-width rows). Confirm exclusion, or specify a different treatment for that surface.
     9	T1: Magnification parameters — radius 200px, max scale 1.4 (lower than the canonical 1.8 because the cards are larger than dock icons), max lift 12px. Confirm or override these tuning numbers before implementation.
    10	T2: Inside an expanded note, the color picker / 3-dot menu popovers must not be clipped during the tween. Plan removes `overflow: hidden` on completion. Do you want a confirmation modal / focus-management before collapsing a note that contains a focused textarea, or is unfocus-then-collapse acceptable?
    11	Cross-cutting: Should the GSAP integrations be feature-flagged behind an env var or a reading-prefs toggle for staged rollout, or are we landing them straight into develop and shipping with the next release?

=== CRITIC: BLOCKERS ===
     1	T5 CRITICAL open question (server-driven routing vs client filtering vs hybrid for /browse, /search, /tag) MUST be answered before any T5 work — the chosen approach changes which files are touched, whether `<Suspense>` boundaries are needed, and whether the `flipBridge` even exists. Cannot begin T5 implementation without this decision.
     2	T1's ChapterCard reference is a non-existent file — the plan must either name the real ChapterList element to tag with `data-dock-item` or explicitly drop chapters from scope. Cannot start T1 until corrected.
     3	T1's homepage hero conversion requires a new client-component file that is NOT in `filesToCreate`. `frontend/app/page.tsx` is a server component (exports metadata) so an inline `'use client'` directive is not an option. Must add `frontend/app/_components/HeroCardsList.tsx` (or similar) to the plan before T1 starts.
     4	T3's QuoteShare integration cites a function signature `onShareClick(target, i, e)` that does not match the current code (no event parameter exists). Must update the plan with the actual signature change and call-site change before T3 ships.
     5	T2's 'always-render both branches' decision is a behaviour change to NoteCard (autosave effects active in every collapsed card). This needs an explicit design decision before T2 implementation — either accept the cost or use a different mount strategy.
     6	T2 must commit to whether `NotesPanel.module.css`'s `.panel.hasExpanded { transition: max-height 260ms }` stays, is removed, or is gated — currently the plan says 'only if needed' but it definitely conflicts with the per-card height tween. Cannot land T2 without resolving this.
     7	T3 ShareButton flash color decision (`--gold-soft` vs `--text-muted` vs new `--share` token) is open. If `--gold-soft` is chosen, globals.css must be added to `filesToChange` to define it across all three theme variants. Block T3 PR until this is decided.

=== CRITIC: GAPS ===
     1	T1 lists `ChapterCard.module.css` and a 'ChapterCard root' in the approach narrative, but no `ChapterCard` component exists in the repo — `frontend/app/series/[id]/_components/ChapterList.tsx` renders chapters inline. The plan must either drop the ChapterCard reference or specify the exact element (an `<a>` inside ChapterList.module.css) that should carry `data-dock-item`.
     2	T1 mentions removing `:hover { transform: translateY(-2px) }` from StoryCard.module.css and ContinueCard.module.css, but does NOT mention `ContinueReadingRow.module.css` line 67-68 (`.card:hover { transform: translateY(-2px) }`) — that file IS in `filesToChange` but the CSS conflict it shares with the dock hook is not enumerated. SeriesCard reuses StoryCard.module.css, so removing the hover translateY there silently removes it from SeriesCard as well — that side effect is not flagged.
     3	T1 fails to list `frontend/components/ChapterList.module.css`, `frontend/components/SeriesCard.module.css` (if separate), or globals.css `--transition-fast` — the per-card `transition: transform var(--transition-fast)` rule on `.card` in StoryCard.module.css will fight every per-frame GSAP write. The risks section calls this out but the `filesToChange` list does not say which lines/properties to scope to `border-color, box-shadow` only.
     4	T1 does not name the integration point for the homepage hero rewrite: `frontend/app/page.tsx` is a server component (it exports `metadata`), so introducing a `'use client'` wrapper requires a NEW client component file (e.g. `frontend/app/_components/HeroCardsList.tsx`) — the plan says 'extract a tiny `use client` wrapper' but lists only `app/page.tsx` and `app/page.module.css` as the touch points, with no new file created. This is a missing file in `filesToCreate`.
     5	T1's NotesPanel attachment misses the mobile sheet codepath: when the panel is in fixed-position sheet mode (under 1100px) the `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` matchMedia gate correctly disables the effect on touch — but on a hybrid 1100px-wide touchscreen laptop the dock will activate over a panel that's also being swiped. No fallback discussed.
     6	T1 omits `frontend/components/ChapterRow` / `ChapterList` analysis — the open question says 'probably should NOT get the dock effect (clarify)' but there's no explicit decision branch in the approach; if it IS excluded, the existing `:hover { transform }` rule there must stay; if it is INCLUDED, ChapterList.tsx and its CSS need to be in `filesToChange`. Plan is ambiguous on the actual edit.
     7	T1 does not list the `frontend/components/InlineRichText` / `TagPill` subtree behaviour: cards contain nested links and pills that themselves have hover states. The hook attaches `pointermove` on the container — children pointer events will still fire on the inner `<TagPill>` which has its own hover styles; no mention of whether `pointer-events: none` is needed on inner decorative elements to keep the proximity computation stable when the cursor briefly passes over a pill at the card edge.
     8	T2 fails to list `frontend/app/admin/_components/NotesPanel.module.css` in `filesToChange`. The panel-level `.panel { transition: max-height 260ms... }` and the `.hasExpanded { min-height: calc(100dvh - 90px); max-height: calc(100dvh - 90px) }` rules combine with the per-card `AutoHeightPanel` height tween: the per-card tween will be measuring its `getBoundingClientRect().height` while the parent panel is mid-transition, producing a wrong `fullH`. The plan calls this 'reconciling … only if needed' — but it WILL be needed and that's not in the DoD.
     9	T2 says to remove `animation: noteExpandIn 200ms`, but doesn't address the per-card `transition: transform 180ms, box-shadow 220ms` on `.card` (NoteCard.module.css lines 18-22). The AutoHeightPanel wraps the body content but the .card itself still has a transform-y transition that the dock hook (T1) will write to — sequencing problem: T1 must remove the transform transition that T2 doesn't touch.
    10	T2 plan to 'always render both branches' inside `<AutoHeightPanel open={expanded}>` will change NoteCard.tsx behavior significantly: title `<input>` and `<textarea>` will be mounted even when collapsed. That means autosave timers, `useEffect` for typing-to-PATCH (lines 76-95) and the menu's outside-click listener will all be running in every collapsed card. Performance + stale-write risk not flagged.
    11	T2's reduced-motion plan calls `gsap.set(el, { height: open ? 'auto' : 0 })` but in the same component the GSAP path uses `overflow: 'hidden'` during tween — the reduced-motion path doesn't set overflow at all, so on the FIRST mount when collapsed, the user will see content overflow before the height collapses (no `overflow: hidden` on the 0-height collapsed state).

T4: Self-contained one-line swap inside an existing hook plus a `lib/gsap.ts` plugin registration; depends on nothing else but unblocks T5 because T5 will also touch `lib/gsap.ts` (Flip registration) — landing T4 first sets the precedent for how new plugins get registered.
T2: Admin-only surface, smallest visual footprint, and the `AutoHeightPanel` component is reusable — landing it before T1 means T1's NotesPanel work can compose with it cleanly (an expanded note inside the dock-list still needs to grow smoothly).
T1: Public-site visual change touching many files; sequencing it after T2 lets the admin notes integration benefit from the AutoHeightPanel already being in place. The shared `useDockProximity` hook is also the first piece of GSAP infrastructure that needs `data-*` attributes on card roots — useful precedent for T5's `data-flip-id`.
T5: Highest-risk and biggest unknown (server-driven routing vs Flip's in-place DOM contract). Saving it for last lets us ship the two purely client-side Flip surfaces (BlockedTagsButton, TagPicker) as a small first PR to prove the integration, then tackle the server-routing flipBridge in a second PR with all other GSAP infrastructure already battle-tested.

=== OPEN QUESTIONS ===
     1	T5 (CRITICAL): The browse/search/tag pages filter server-side via App Router navigation, so cards are brand-new React/DOM nodes on each filter click. Are you OK with this risk profile, or would you rather (a) convert /search and /tag to client-side filtering (loses SSR result counts, breaks /tag/[slug] SEO landing), or (b) hybrid (over-fetch + client filter + reconcile, most work, smoothest UX)?      4	T4: Tween duration of 1.1s with `power2.out` and `autoKill: true` is the default; do you want a distance-aware duration (longer trips take ~1.6s, short ~0.6s) or a fixed 1.1s for everyone?

content.text:
The plan + critique is in. Honest summary of what came back — the research workflow caught a few real bugs in my own plan that I want you to weigh in on before I create any issues or write any code.

## Research outcomes
- **GSAP is fully free** post-2024 Webflow acquisition (incl. all premium plugins). No license blocker.
- **macOS dock demo couldn't be fetched** — `demos.gsap.com` is just a wrapper around a CodePen that 403'd. The technique is well-known so the plan reconstructs it from canonical knowledge (single `pointermove` on container, per-card distance→scale falloff, `gsap.quickTo` for throughput).
- **Auto-height demo** ✅ measure-then-tween (`scrollHeight` + `gsap.fromTo({height:startH},{height:fullH})`, set `auto` on complete).
- **ScrollToPlugin** confirmed for T4 — free, single-line tween.
- **Flip plugin** confirmed for T5 — but tag filtering is **server-side** in this app, which complicates it.
- **`useGSAP` from `@gsap/react`** is the right hook everywhere; cleanup is automatic via `context.revert()`.

## The 5 tasks (suggested implementation order)

| # | Task | Plugin | PRs | Why this slot |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **T3** Like/Save/Share click feedback + per-button color | core | 1 | Smallest, most isolated. Proves the `useGSAP` + `contextSafe` pattern the rest reuse. |
| **2** | **T4** Smooth scroll-restore to last reading position | ScrollToPlugin | 1 | One-line swap in an existing hook. Lands the new-plugin registration pattern. |
| **3** | **T2** Animate auto-height when expanding a note | core | 1 | Admin-only, small footprint. The `AutoHeightPanel` becomes reusable infrastructure for T1's notes integration. |
| **4** | **T1** Dock-proximity hover on all card rows + notes list | core | 2 | Many files. Public-side visual change. Composes with T2 cleanly. |
| **5** | **T5** Flip reorder on tag filtering | Flip | 2 | Highest risk (server routing vs Flip's same-DOM contract). Saved for last with infra warmed up. |

## ⚠️ Decisions I need from you before any code

The critic flagged **7 blockers + 29 gaps + 21 revisions**. Most are details I can resolve in implementation. But these need your call — they change scope or design:

**A. T5 — the big one.** Tag filtering is server-side (URL navigation). Flip needs the same DOM elements before/after. Three options:
- **(a)** Server-side + a module-level `flipBridge` Map carrying Flip state across the navigation. **Lightest, but fragile** if React doesn't preserve the grid container across server renders. Plan's default.
- **(b)** Convert `/search` to client-side filtering. Smoothest UX but loses SSR result counts and `/tag/[slug]` SEO landings.
- **(c)** Hybrid: over-fetch + client filter + reconcile. Most work, best result.

**B. T5 scope** — `/tag/[slug]` pages would need a different mechanism (separate route). Plan defaults to **out of scope** for now (only TagBar reorders on `/search`). OK?

**C. T3 — ShareButton's flash color.** Like is `--like` (red), Save is `--gold`. Share has no obvious token. Pick: **`--text-muted`** (neutral, no token cost) · **`--gold-soft`** (matches Save family — but the token doesn't exist yet, would need to define) · **new `--share` token** in `globals.css`.

**D. T2 — when an expanded note collapses, should both branches always be mounted** (so autosave timers keep running in collapsed cards — slight perf cost) **or unmount-on-collapse** (clean but the auto-height tween needs a different mount strategy)?

**E. T1 NotesPanel dock orientation.** The panel's pill list is **vertical** (`flex-direction: column`). A real macOS dock is horizontal. Vertical dock is technically fine but reads less iconically. Accept vertical, or rotate the list horizontal first (would conflict with the panel's `overflow-y` scroll)?

**F. T1 dock-effect tuning.** Defaults: **radius 200px, max scale 1.4, max lift 12px** (toned down from the canonical 1.8/20 because story cards are bigger than dock icons). OK or rebalance?

**G. T1 chapters.** `/series/[id]` shows chapters as a vertical full-width list (not a rail). Plan **excludes** them from the dock — full-width row magnification would look broken. Confirm exclude.

**H. T4 hash precedence.** If a returning reader arrives via a `#:~:text=…` shared quote URL, **text-fragment wins** (skip scroll restore entirely). Confirm.

**I. T4 tween duration.** Fixed **1.1s `power2.out`** for everyone, or distance-aware (long trips ~1.6s, short ~0.6s)?

**J. Feature-flag the whole set?** Land in `develop` and ship on next deploy (current default), or gate each behind an env var / settings toggle for staged rollout (especially T5 — has the most production risk)?

## Real bugs the critic caught in my plan (I'll fix regardless of your answers)

- T1 mentioned a `ChapterCard` component that **doesn't exist** — chapters are inline in `ChapterList`.
- T1's homepage hero conversion needs a **new client-component wrapper file** (`app/page.tsx` is a server component with `metadata`); plan listed only edits, no new file.
- T3's QuoteShare integration referenced `onShareClick(target, i, e)` — the **actual signature has no event arg**; needs widening or a per-button ref instead.
- T2 doesn't list `NotesPanel.module.css` in files-to-change — but the panel-level `max-height` transition **will race** the per-card height tween.
- T3 plans to tween a CSS custom property via `box-shadow` — needs **`@property` registration** in `globals.css` for smooth interpolation, otherwise it'll snap.

## Once you answer A–J:

1. I'll fold the critic's revisions into the plan (drop the ghost `ChapterCard`, add the hero wrapper file, widen the QuoteShare signature, etc.).
2. Create **5 GitHub Issues** (with `gh issue create`, labels `gsap` + `enhancement`, milestone "GSAP integration").
3. Ship task by task — **T3 → T4 → T2 → T1 → T5** — each its own PR(s) into `develop`, each its own sandbox-tested branch, your normal review-on-dev gate.

Take the questions in any order — even just answering A and C would unblock me to start on T3 + T4 while we work out the rest.

=== T4 ISSUE BODY (first task in sequence — preview) ===
## What
Replace the instant `window.scrollTo` at `frontend/lib/useReadingPosition.ts:119` with a GSAP `ScrollToPlugin` tween so returning readers glide back to their saved position.

## Decisions (committed)
- **Duration**: 1.1s fixed, no distance-aware scaling
- **Ease**: `power2.out`
- **autoKill**: `true` (default for window targets — any user wheel/touch/key input cancels the tween instantly, which is the whole point)
- **Hash precedence**: ANY non-empty `window.location.hash` — especially text fragments like `#:~:text=...` — wins; skip the tween and let the browser handle the anchor/fragment
- **Reduced motion**: skip the tween, retain the existing `behavior: 'instant'` scrollTo
- **Tween storage**: `const tweenRef = useRef<gsap.core.Tween | null>(null)` so the existing cleanup return can `tweenRef.current?.kill()`
- **ScrollTrigger coordination**: pass `onUpdate: () => ScrollTrigger.update()` so any ScrollTrigger-driven reveals on the page fire correctly during the programmatic scroll
- **Write-throttle pause**: `const restoringRef = useRef(false)`; set true immediately before launching the tween; in `onScroll`, early-return when true; clear via `onAutoKill | onComplete | onInterrupt`. Prevents 100+ wasted PATCH calls during the 1.1s tween (the existing `WRITE_THROTTLE_MS = 5000` only kicks in after the first write)

- `frontend/lib/useReadingPosition.ts` (line 119 + surrounding effect)
- `frontend/lib/gsap.ts` (register ScrollToPlugin)

- [ ] Flick the wheel mid-restore — tween aborts instantly (autoKill)
- [ ] Hit PageDown mid-restore — tween aborts (autoKill catches keyboard too)
- [ ] Open /chapter/[id]#some-heading — instant anchor jump, no tween

What this is

This is my diary — the place I keep my darkest and most erotic fantasies. Every entry is something I actually wanted to write down: open-door and explicit, dark and filthy, or slow, deep, and romantic. They don’t all live in the same mood, because neither do I.

Every word here is mine. This isn’t an anthology or a submission feed — it’s one author, one voice, writing in their spare time, by hand. New pages go up when they’re ready, so updates take a while. That’s the point. Nothing here is churned out. This isn’t a wall of throwaway smut. Each entry is adult fiction with craft behind it: sex stories that earn their heat, erotic series that take their time, and characters worth following into the dark. Every piece waited until it was worth confessing — and it’s written to be read, not skimmed.

{/* ── Feature trio ─────────────────────────────────────── */}

Stories & series

Standalone erotic tales for a single restless sitting, and multi-chapter slow-burn series for the nights you want the tension to build and build. Whether you came for a quick spicy read or a slow-burn erotic romance that unravels across dozens of chapters, you’ll find adult short fiction here that treats desire as something worth writing well.

Read anonymously

No sign-up to start reading. Leave a like, save your place, pick up where you left off — an account is optional, never the price of admission. This site is anonymous by design: no tracking, no data harvesting, no name to hand over. Read like no one’s watching, because no one is.

Browse by tag

Every story is tagged by theme and kink, so whatever you’re in the mood for — soft and spicy or genuinely filthy, romantic or dark — the catalog bends to your taste. Filter by mood, length, heat level, and content so you always know what you’re walking into.

content.text:
I have to push back on the scraping part, but the goal — populating dev with enough stories/series to stress-test the GSAP work — is completely valid and there's a better way to get there.

## Why I can't pull from Literotica (or similar)

Their content is copyrighted, and their ToS prohibit redistribution. **Even storing scraped content on a private dev server is infringement** — copyright doesn't have a "but it's not public" exception. There's also the precedent problem: if I'll scrape "for dev," it muddies what's a fair thing to ask me to do. I'd rather just not, especially with such a clean alternative right there.

## What actually tests the GSAP work better

For the five animations, the *content* doesn't matter — what matters is **the shape of the data**: card volume, tag distributions, excerpt lengths, scroll-able body lengths, a few `isAuthorsChoice` flags, a mix of adult/safe tags. That's exactly what a **synthetic seed script** generates, and it tests the animations more rigorously than real content because I can engineer the edge cases (a 50-tag story, a story with a 30-line excerpt, a series with 25 chapters, etc.).

## The plan

A Prisma seed script (`backend/scripts/seed-dev-content.ts`) that:

| Generates | Volume | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Standalone stories** | 50 | Varied lengths (~500–10k words of literary-flavored lorem), 3–6 tags each from your existing 591-tag taxonomy, mix of adult / safe / authors-choice, `publishedAt` spread across the past 6 months |
| **Series** | 8 | Mix of ONGOING / COMPLETE / HIATUS, each with 3–8 chapters, series-level tags plus per-chapter tags |
| **Chapters total** | ~40 | Belong to the series above, varied lengths, proper `orderIndex` |
| **Tag distribution** | uses your real tags | Stress-tests T5 Flip-reorder across many filter combos and the homepage rails' tag pills |
| **Idempotent** | yes | Marks each row with a `[seed]` prefix in a comment field so a `--purge` flag can wipe *just* the seeded rows |

**Safety rails:**
- Requires an explicit `--confirm=dev` CLI flag; running without it prints a warning and exits.
- Refuses to run if `DATABASE_URL` doesn't pass a sanity check the user wires up (e.g., a `LUCIFER_ENV=dev` env var must also be set).
- Ships in `backend/scripts/`, **not** a Prisma migration — never auto-runs on `prisma migrate deploy`, never touches prod.
- All seeded rows tagged with a hidden marker so `npx ts-node backend/scripts/seed-dev-content.ts --purge` cleanly removes them with no manual SQL.

## What you'd do once it's merged

On the dev server only:
```bash
LUCIFER_ENV=dev npx ts-node backend/scripts/seed-dev-content.ts --confirm=dev
```

50 stories + 8 series materialize. GSAP animations have something to magnify, scroll through, filter, and Flip-reorder. The script never reaches prod because (a) you don't run it there, and (b) the env-guard would refuse anyway.

## Want me to build it?

Say **yes** and I'll branch off `develop`, build the seed script + the purge flag, wire the safety guards, sandbox-test (compile + a dry-run that prints what it'd insert without writing), and open a PR. Or if you want different volumes / shapes (more series, fewer stories, specific tag combos to focus on certain GSAP behaviors), tell me what to tune.

Sticking with the no — but let me be clear *why* X/Reddit don't solve this, and then redirect to what does. Quick:

## The "X / Reddit / fair use" idea doesn't work

- **Every post is copyrighted from the moment it's written.** A random user's tweet or Reddit comment is theirs, full stop. Neither platform gives third parties a blanket license to re-host that content. "There's a lot of it" doesn't change who owns it.
- **Fair use isn't a category I can pre-clear.** It's a defense argued case-by-case in court (purpose, amount, market effect…). "I think this is fair use" is not the same as "this is safe to scrape and store." For stress-testing UI, it's not fair use anyway — there's no transformative purpose.
- **Both platforms' ToS forbid scraping.** Reddit changed its API in 2023 specifically to stop third-party copy. X charges money for the API and litigates scrapers. Bypassing those would put you (and me, by association) on the wrong side of the platforms.
- **Public-domain erotica does exist** (older works on Project Gutenberg, etc.) — but it's a tiny pool, the *shape* (Victorian-era novellas) won't match your brand or your tag taxonomy, and using it just to test animations is wildly disproportionate effort. Wrong tool.

## Same goal, the right tool

For testing the GSAP work, **content doesn't matter — shape does**. Volume of cards, length of titles/excerpts, tag-distribution density, body length for the scroll-restore tween. Synthetic data hits those metrics **on purpose** — I can engineer the edge cases real content can't (a 50-tag story to stress T5; a 25-chapter series; a 30-line excerpt). I'd use `@faker-js/faker` for filler + a small hand-written pool of evocative titles/excerpts that match your brand voice (suggestive, not explicit — animations don't need explicit text).

Concretely, the same plan I proposed last turn:

```
backend/scripts/seed-dev-content.ts
  50 standalone stories · 8 series (3–8 chapters each) · ~40 chapters total
  Real tags from your existing 591-tag taxonomy, varied combos
  Adult / safe mix · isAuthorsChoice flags · publishedAt spread over 6 months
  Idempotent · --confirm=dev flag · --purge flag · env-guard refuses non-dev DBs
  Faker-driven body length variance (500–10k words) for the scroll-restore tween
```

**Say "go" and I'll build it now** — research best Prisma seed patterns + faker integration via a Workflow, design the script, sandbox-test (compile + dry-run mode that prints what *would* insert), open a PR into `develop`. You run it on the dev DB once. Done.

(If you want a different angle entirely — e.g. "I'll provide 5 of my own real stories as a template, and you generate variations on those" — that works too. Tell me.)

=== DECISION SUMMARY ===
The verified public-domain erotica pool is real but tiny (~15-25 unique English titles), almost entirely pre-1930, and reads as florid Victorian/Enlightenment euphemism with consent vocabularies that range from absent to actively offensive — using any of it in UI fixtures would actively undermine the contemporary slow-burn-literary brand. For the actual test goal (stressing GSAP scroll animations across PRs #187-#191, which care about page length and scroll distance, not prose semantics), a synthetic faker-driven seeder is both safer and more fit-for-purpose. The synthetic plan is fully spec'd, safety-guarded, idempotent, and ready to ship as a single PR.

=== PD OPTION ===
viable: false
volume: ~15-25 unique English-language literary-erotica works total across PG bookshelves 33 + 703, Wikisource, and PDR. Modern CC0/PD erotica is effectively a null set. Anything on Internet Archive labeled 'free to read' that isn't sourced from PG is in-copyright and a DMCA trap.
voice fit: Bad. Every usable title is pre-1930, most are Victorian or earlier (Fanny Hill 1748, Venus in Furs 1870, Decameron 1350s, Teleny 1893, The Pearl 1879). Voice is florid period euphemism that reads as parody to contemporary eyes and clashes with the Garth-Greenwell/Mary-Gaitskill register the site is going for. Consent and queer-affirming vocabularies are absent; several titles (The Pearl, Venus in India, Moorish Harem) carry colonial-fetish and non-consent content that's ethically fraught to surface in any UI.
fit for GSAP testing: Mediocre even on the narrow technical goal. GSAP work cares about page length, scroll distance, and tag-density spread across stories/series/chapters — not prose authenticity. PD bodies exist (Decameron, Casanova/Machen) but ingestion, cleanup, and chunking into chapter-shaped units is meaningful engineering for content that you'd then have to hide from the UI anyway because it's brand-toxic. Synthetic lorem of controlled length hits the same animation surface with zero ingestion overhead.
recommendation: skip

=== SYNTHETIC OPTION ===
file: Single new file at backend/scripts/seed-dev-content.ts following the existing seed:* convention (sibling of seed-tags.ts and seed-content.ts, ts-node --transpile-only, idempotent main()/catch/disconnect lifecycle). Adds @faker-js/faker as a devDependency in backend/package.json and a `seed:dev` script entry. No schema migration — the [seed-dev] title prefix is the marker, so purge is a trivial startsWith filter.
volume: 50 standalone stories + 8 series with 3-8 chapters each (averages ~44 chapters, within the 40-60 envelope). Each body is 500-10,000 words uniform-random to give the GSAP scroll work a healthy spread of short/medium/long pages. Tags pulled live from the DB's 591-tag taxonomy: 3-6 per row, 70/30 safe/adult mix so the distribution matches the rough real-site shape. Titles are hand-pooled mood words combined with faker — brand-aligned, never copied. Bodies are pure faker.lorem because animation work doesn't care about semantics.
safety: Three independent guards: (1) hard refuse unless LUCIFER_ENV=dev, (2) sniff DATABASE_URL for prod/production/render.com/neon.tech and abort if matched, (3) require --confirm=dev on every seed run. Idempotent — refuses to seed if [seed-dev] rows already exist, points operator at --purge. --purge wipes ONLY rows whose title starts with [seed-dev] (Story/Series/Chapter), inside a single transaction, with cascades handling junction tables. --dry-run prints counts + first 5 titles per type with zero writes. All inserts wrapped in one prisma.$transaction (120s timeout) so a mid-run crash leaves zero partial rows. Strict exit codes: 0 success, 1 guard failure, 2 runtime error.
run: cd backend && LUCIFER_ENV=dev npm run seed:dev -- --confirm=dev
purge: cd backend && LUCIFER_ENV=dev npm run seed:dev -- --purge

=== RECOMMENDATION ===
synthetic

=== READY TO BUILD: true ===

=== WHAT BUILD LOOKS LIKE ===
     1	Add @faker-js/faker to backend/package.json devDependencies (npm i -D @faker-js/faker in backend/) and a new `seed:dev` script entry pointing at scripts/seed-dev-content.ts via ts-node --transpile-only.
     2	Create /Users/taha/Claude projects/LucifersDiary/backend/scripts/seed-dev-content.ts implementing the full skeleton: CLI parsing, three safety guards (LUCIFER_ENV, DATABASE_URL sniff, --confirm=dev), tag-bucket loader, planners for stories/series/chapters, transactional insert, --purge path, --dry-run reporter.
     3	Zero schema changes — the [seed-dev] title prefix is the marker, exported as a top-level SEED_MARKER constant so seed and purge can't drift.
     4	No changes to existing seed-tags.ts or seed-content.ts — this is a new sibling script with its own namespace.
     5	After merge the user runs (from backend/): LUCIFER_ENV=dev npm run seed:dev -- --confirm=dev to populate, --dry-run to preview, --purge to wipe. Then opens the GSAP-scroll PRs against a DB with 50 stories + 8 series + ~44 chapters of varied length.
     6	Optional follow-ups (out of scope for this PR): a tiny docs/dev-seeding.md note pointing at the script, and a CI guard that fails if anyone tries to import @faker-js/faker outside scripts/.

=== OPEN QUESTIONS ===
     1	Keep the default counts (50 stories / 8 series / 3-8 chapters each) or push higher for heavier scroll-stress?
     2	Should the script also seed a handful of draft (publishedAt=null) rows so the admin draft views are exercised, or published-only as currently specced?
     3	Lock in the [seed-dev] title prefix as the marker, or would you rather a less-visible tag (e.g. a specific authorsNote sentinel) so the prefix doesn't appear if a screenshot leaks?

=== PD: OVERALL VERDICT ===
PD content is NOT a viable path for Lucifer's Diary fixtures if the goal is voice-representative test data. The honest landscape: roughly 15-25 unique English-language literary-erotica works are reliably PD (Fanny Hill, Venus in Furs, Decameron, Casanova/Machen, Teleny, The Pearl, Romance of Lust, My Secret Life, Sade selections, Frank Harris, Autobiography of a Flea, plus a handful of erotic poetry — Sappho, Catullus, Goethe's Roman Elegies). Every single one is pre-1930, most are Victorian or earlier, and they share three disqualifying traits for a modern slow-burn-literary-erotica fixture pool: (1) florid period-specific euphemism that reads as parody to contemporary eyes, (2) consent and sexual-politics vocabularies that are absent or actively offensive (colonial fetish, racism, non-consent framed as titillation), and (3) tag-taxonomy mismatch — a 591-tag modern system built around contemporary kink/identity/consent discourse cannot meaningfully tag Victorian clandestine prose without force-fitting. Three practical paths forward, ranked: (1) BEST: commission a small (~20-50 piece) original fixture corpus from a freelance erotica writer with a work-for-hire / CC0 release — gives voice fidelity, tag fidelity, and unambiguous license. (2) ACCEPTABLE: generate synthetic fixture text with an LLM specifically for fixture-display purposes (clearly labeled as synthetic, not as real content). (3) WORST but cheapest: use the PG corpus for STRUCTURAL fixtures only (chapter counts, word counts, tag density) without ever surfacing the actual prose in UI. Do NOT mix Victorian PD prose into anything a real user would see — it will undermine the contemporary brand. The Standard Ebooks 'we curate PD with editorial polish' model is not a shortcut here because they correctly don't curate erotica. Internet Archive's 'free to read' is a copyright trap, not a source. CC0 modern erotica is essentially a null set.

=== PD: MODERN PD EXISTS? ===
No. There is no usable pool of CC0 or verified-public-domain MODERN erotic fiction online. After surveying Creative Commons indexes, Project Gutenberg post-1929 holdings, Standard Ebooks, Wikisource, Internet Archive, and Public Domain Review, the available verified-PD corpus is overwhelmingly pre-1930 (most of it pre-1900), with voice and tag vocabularies that do not match a contemporary literary-erotica site. Contemporary authors essentially never release erotica under CC0 — the genre's economics (paid platforms, Patreon, indie publishing) and stigma both push the opposite direction. The 'modern free erotica' that exists online is either (a) author-promo content still under copyright, (b) Controlled-Digital-Lending material on IA that is legally contested and NOT public domain, or (c) unlicensed/pirated. None of these are safe as fixture sources.

- REQUIRED: seriesId (FK -> Series.id), title (String), content (String), excerpt (String), orderIndex (Int — manual, no default; pick max+1 per series), estimatedReadMinutes (Int).
- Has defaults: isAuthorsChoice (false), accumulatedReadSeconds (0), likeCount (0).
- Optional/nullable: epigraph, authorsNote, publishedAt (null = draft), deletedAt.
- Tags via ChapterTag { chapterId, tagId } — composite PK.
- Do NOT write: searchVector.

- POST /admin/stories (CreateStoryDto, backend/src/stories/dto/create-story.dto.ts): required title, content, excerpt, estimatedReadMinutes; optional isAuthorsChoice, authorsNote, epigraph, tagIds (UUID[]). Then PATCH /admin/stories/:id/publish to publish.
